senses.title: An official document that allows an activity
senses.definition: a document issued by an authority that gives a person or a business the right to do something
senses.definitionCN: 由主管机关发放、赋予个人或企业做某事的权利的证件
senses.example: He showed his driving licence to the officer.
senses.exampleCN: 他把驾驶执照出示给警官。
senses.why: Latin licentia named permission, and a licence is that permission made visible as paper, so the abstract right and the card in a wallet are the same sense at two stages.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 licentia 指的就是许可，而 licence 是把那份许可变成看得见的纸；因此抽象的权利与钱包里的卡片，是同一个义项的两个阶段。

senses.title: Formal permission to do something
senses.definition: official or formal permission, whether or not it comes with a document
senses.definitionCN: 正式或官方的准许，无论是否附有证件
senses.example: The film was shown under licence from the studio.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影获得制片公司许可后才放映。
senses.why: Strip away the paper and what remains is the permission itself; the word then names the granting rather than the certificate.
senses.whyCN: 把纸去掉，剩下的就是许可本身；此时这个词指的是「准许」这件行为，而不是那张证书。

senses.title: Freedom to behave beyond the usual limits
senses.definition: the freedom to act without restraint, often used when the freedom has gone too far
senses.definitionCN: 不受约束地行事的自由，常用于指这种自由已经过了头
senses.example: The novel's licence with facts annoyed historians.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说对史实的随意处理让历史学家不满。
senses.why: Permission with no one setting its edges turns into boldness; the same noun slides from an allowed act to an excess that others resent.
senses.whyCN: 一旦没有人给许可划边界，准许就变成大胆妄为；同一个名词从「被允许的行为」滑向「让别人不满的过头」。

senses.title: Special freedom granted to an artist or writer
senses.definition: the accepted freedom of a writer or artist to change facts or break rules for effect
senses.definitionCN: 作家或艺术家为效果而改动事实、打破常规时被认可的自由
senses.example: Poetic licence let the songwriter bend the grammar.
senses.exampleCN: 诗歌的特许自由让这位词作者改动了语法。
senses.why: The narrowest sense is a professional allowance: art is permitted to depart from fact, and the word keeps the same frame of granted freedom.
senses.whyCN: 最窄的义项是一种职业上的照顾：艺术被允许偏离事实，而这个词仍然保留「被授予的自由」这一框架。

intro.en: Licence comes from a Latin verb for being allowed, through its abstract noun, and the noun arrived in English by way of French with the sense of leave or permission.
intro.cn: licence 来自拉丁语中表示「被允许」的动词，经它的抽象名词，再由法语以「准许、许可」的意思进入英语。

items.en: Licere meant to be allowed or to be permitted, and it described what a person might lawfully do.
items.cn: licere 意为被允许、获准，描述一个人可以合法地做什么。

items.en: Licentia was the noun for freedom or permission, and it could also name boldness that oversteps.
items.cn: licentia 是表示自由或许可的名词，也可以指越界的大胆。

items.en: Old French took the noun as licence, meaning leave or permission, and handed it to English.
items.cn: 古法语把这个名词作 licence，意为准许或许可，并传给了英语。

items.en: Middle English licence covers a granted privilege, a formal permission and the freedom of behaviour.
items.cn: 中古英语的 licence 覆盖被授予的特权、正式的许可，以及行为上的自由。

items.en: Modern English keeps licence as the British noun and license as the American spelling, while the verb is license everywhere.
items.cn: 现代英语保留英式名词 licence 与美式拼写 license，而动词在各地都写作 license。

definition_zh: 盖子；眼睑；限制；压制
definition_en: a removable cover for a container; also the fold of skin over the eye, or a check placed on something
core_image: 一只手捏住锅盖的提钮，把热气和味道扣在锅里
scene: 厨房里热气腾腾，锅里的汤咕嘟作响。She lifted the lid and let the steam escape.
sceneCN: 这里是「盖子」（第 1 个义项：容器的盖）；句意为她掀开锅盖，让蒸汽散出去。图中可辨识物件：汤锅、木质锅盖、灶火。

derivatives.zh: 由 eye 与 lid 复合而成，义为「眼皮；眼睑」
由 lid 加表示「没有」的后缀 -less 构成，义为「无盖的；没有眼皮的」
由 lid 加表示「具有」的后缀 -ed 构成，义为「带盖的」

senses.title: A cover for a container
senses.definition: a removable cover that fits over the top of a pot, box or other container
senses.definitionCN: 盖在锅、箱等容器顶部、可以取下的盖
senses.example: She lifted the lid of the pot and stirred the soup.
senses.exampleCN: 她掀开锅盖，搅了搅汤。
senses.why: The oldest sense names the thing that closes a container; Old English hlid meant a covering that keeps what is inside in place.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项指「把容器合上的东西」；古英语 hlid 就指覆盖物，作用是让里面的东西留在原处。

senses.title: Either fold of skin over the eye
senses.definition: one of the two movable folds of skin that close over the eye
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖在眼球上、可以开合的两片皮肤之一
senses.example: His lids grew heavy as the film went on.
senses.exampleCN: 电影越放越久，他的眼皮越发沉重。
senses.why: Closing the eye is covering it, so the same word for a cover was extended to the fold that covers the eyeball.
senses.whyCN: 合眼就是把眼睛盖上，于是原本表示覆盖物的词，被用来指遮住眼球的那层皮。

senses.title: A check or limit on something
senses.definition: a limit that keeps an activity, price or piece of news under control
senses.definitionCN: 把某项活动、价格或消息控制住的界限
senses.example: The mayor promised to keep a lid on city spending.
senses.exampleCN: 市长承诺要管住市里的开支。
senses.why: A lid seals a container, and in speech the image becomes a seal on spending or news, so the word names control rather than a physical cover.
senses.whyCN: 盖子能把容器封住；用到言语里，被封住的对象变成开支或消息，于是这个词表示「控住」，而不是实物盖子。

intro.en: Lid is an Old English word for a cover, and its eye and restraint senses grow out of the same act of closing something.
intro.cn: lid 是古英语里表示覆盖物的词，眼睑与「压制」两个义项都从「把东西合上」这个动作长出来。

items.en: A reconstructed noun for a covering is believed to stand behind the Old English word, though its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为古英语词背后有一个表示覆盖物的原始日耳曼语名词，但更深层的来源不确定。

items.en: Hlid named a cover for a container, and it could also name the covering of the eye.
items.cn: hlid 指容器的盖，也可以指眼睛上的那层覆盖。

items.en: Middle English kept lid for both the pot cover and the eyelid, and the spelling settled without the initial h.
items.cn: 中古英语的 lid 同时指锅盖与眼皮，拼写定型下来，词首的 h 不再写出。

items.en: The word spread from kitchens to workshops and became the ordinary noun for any removable cover.
items.cn: 这个词从厨房走进作坊，成为任何可取下盖子的常用名词。

items.en: Modern English adds a figurative restraint, so that a budget or a rumour can be sealed like a pot.
items.cn: 现代英语给它添上一层比喻性的「压制」，使预算或传闻也能像锅一样被封住。

note.en: The first group collects words built on the same cover image or close in spelling; the second collects other names for covers.
note.cn: 第一组收同一「覆盖」意象或拼写相近的词；第二组收其他表示覆盖物的词。

entries.definition: The fold of skin that covers the eye, built from eye and lid.
entries.definitionCN: 由 eye 与 lid 复合而成，指覆盖眼睛的那层皮，即眼皮。

entries.definitionCN: 没有盖子的，或没有眼皮的。

entries.definitionCN: 盖在上面起保护或封闭作用的东西；盖子。

entries.definition: A small lid or top for a bottle or pen.
entries.definitionCN: 瓶口或笔端的小盖。

entries.definition: A plug that closes the mouth of a bottle or tube.
entries.definitionCN: 塞住瓶口或管口的塞子。

normalIntro.en: Lid is a short Old English word for a cover, and its family keeps the picture of something closing over an opening.
normalIntro.cn: lid 是古英语里表示覆盖物的短词，它的同族词都保留「把开口合上」的画面。

normal.en: Old English hlid meant a cover, and the h simply dropped away in Middle English.
normal.cn: 古英语 hlid 意为覆盖物，到了中古英语，词首的 h 就消失了。

normal.en: Eyelid is eye plus lid: the lid that covers the eye.
normal.cn: eyelid 是 eye 加 lid，即盖住眼睛的那片「盖子」。

normal.en: Lidless drops the cover, so it means having no lid or no eyelids.
normal.cn: lidless 去掉盖子，所以表示没有盖子或没有眼皮。

normal.en: Keep a lid on turns a kitchen cover into a limit on money, noise or news.
normal.cn: keep a lid on 把厨房的盖子变成对钱、声音或消息的限制。

normal.en: A pot lid and a dustbin lid differ only in what they seal, not in the shape of the word.
normal.cn: 锅盖与垃圾桶盖不同的只是封住什么，词形本身不变。

abstract.en: Anything that can be opened has a lid, which is why the word moves so easily from pots to eyes to budgets.
abstract.cn: 凡是可以打开的东西都有盖子，所以这个词能轻易从锅移到眼睛，再移到预算。

abstract.en: A lid does not hide what is inside; it keeps it from escaping, and that is the link between cover and control.
abstract.cn: 盖子并不隐藏里面的东西，而是不让它跑出来，这正是「覆盖」与「控制」之间的连接。

abstract.en: The word is short and shut like the thing it names, a small sound that closes a container.
abstract.cn: 这个词又短又闭合，像它所指的东西，一个短短的音就把容器合上。

examples.en: She lifted the lid of the pot and stirred the soup.
examples.cn: 她掀开锅盖，搅了搅汤。

examples.en: His lids felt heavy after the long drive.
examples.cn: 长途开车之后，他的眼皮沉得厉害。

examples.en: The coach kept a lid on the team's excitement before the final.
examples.cn: 决赛前，教练压住了队员们的兴奋情绪。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「离得」——盖子离得开，才装得下东西；lid 就是盖子。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a cover that closes an opening; the senses spread to the cover of the eye and then to any limit that keeps something under control.

branches.cn: 蒸汽被锅盖压住

branches.en: a blink that shuts the eye for a moment
branches.cn: 一次眨眼把眼睛短暂合上

branches.en: a child rubbing heavy lids at bedtime

definition_zh: 躺；平卧；位于；撒谎；谎言
definition_en: to be in a flat resting position; to be situated; to say something untrue; an untrue statement
core_image: 身体放平，静卧不动；或嘴一张，假话滑出
scene: 午后阳台，猫在毯子上翻了个身。The old town lies beside a quiet river.
sceneCN: 这里 lie 是「位于」（第 2 个义项：坐落、位于）；句意为古城坐落在一条安静的河边。

derivatives.zh: lie 加指人后缀 -ar，指「说谎的人」
lie 加 -ing，指「说谎的；躺卧的」

senses.title: To be in a flat resting position
senses.definition: to put your body flat on a surface to rest
senses.definitionCN: 把身体平放在一个面上休息
senses.example: The cat lies on the warm mat all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 猫整个下午都躺在暖垫上。
senses.why: A body laid out flat is the plain physical picture.
senses.whyCN: 平放的身体是最直白的画面。

senses.title: To be situated
senses.definition: to be in a particular place or position
senses.definitionCN: 处于某地或某位置
senses.example: The old town lies beside a quiet river.
senses.exampleCN: 古城坐落在安静的河边。
senses.why: A place 'rests' where it is, so the body word extends to geography.
senses.whyCN: 地方「安卧」于其所在，身体之词便延伸到地理。

senses.title: To stay or remain in a state
senses.definition: to remain in a specified condition
senses.definitionCN: 保持于特定状态
senses.example: The papers lay untouched for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 文件一周没人碰。
senses.why: What lies somewhere also lies in some state; position and condition share the verb.
senses.whyCN: 躺于某处也即处于某状态，位置与状态共用此动词。

senses.title: To say something untrue
senses.definition: to make a false statement on purpose
senses.definitionCN: 故意作虚假陈述
senses.example: He lied about his age to join.
senses.exampleCN: 他谎报年龄报名。
senses.why: The mouth builds a false picture; a different verb grew beside the lying-down one.
senses.whyCN: 嘴构建假象；这个词与「躺卧」的词是并肩长成的另一个词。

senses.title: An untrue statement
senses.definition: something said that is known to be false
senses.definitionCN: 明知不实而言之事
senses.example: That story is a bare-faced lie.
senses.exampleCN: 那个说法是彻头彻尾的谎言。
senses.why: The false statement freezes into a noun anyone can point at.
senses.whyCN: 假陈述凝固成名词，人人可以指认。

senses.title: To be about to happen (lie ahead)
senses.definition: to be waiting in the future
senses.definitionCN: 在将来等待
senses.example: Greater tests lie ahead of us.
senses.exampleCN: 更大的考验在前方等着我们。
senses.why: The future stretches out before you like a road you have not walked.
senses.whyCN: 未来像未走的路在你面前铺开。

senses.title: To be buried or at rest (lie)
senses.definition: to be buried in a grave or resting place
senses.definitionCN: 安葬于墓穴或安息之所
senses.example: Her ashes lie beneath the old oak.
senses.exampleCN: 她的骨灰安放在老橡树下。
senses.why: Final rest is the last lying down, the verb\u0027s quietest use.
senses.whyCN: 最终安息是最后一次躺下，动词最安静的用法。

intro.en: Two verbs share the spelling lie. The posture word comes from Old English licgan, from Germanic ligan 'to lie down'; the falsehood word comes from Old English leogan 'to tell lies', from a root meaning 'to lie, be false'.
intro.cn: 两个动词共用拼写 lie。姿态词来自古英语 licgan，出自日耳曼语 ligan「躺下」；谎言词来自古英语 leogan「说谎」，词根意为「不实」。

items.en: Old English licgan meant 'to lie, be situated', the posture verb used across English ever since.
items.cn: 古英语 licgan 意为「躺、位于」，姿态动词沿用至今。

items.en: Germanic ligan is behind the posture verb, kin to German liegen and Dutch liggen.
items.cn: 日耳曼语 ligan 是姿态动词的来源，与德语 liegen、荷兰语 liggen 同族。

items.en: Old English leogan meant 'to tell falsehoods', a separate verb with its own root.
items.cn: 古英语 leogan 意为「说谎」，是与姿态词无关的独立动词。

items.en: The falsehood root spread through Germanic, giving German lugen 'to peer, spy' in some dialects.
items.cn: 谎言词根遍布日耳曼语族，某些方言给出德语 lugen「窥视」。

items.en: In Middle English the two verbs kept distinct past forms while sharing one spelling.
items.cn: 中古英语里两动词过去式分立，仅共享一个拼写。

note.en: Group one flags the famous confusions; group two lists rest and falsehood words.
note.cn: 第一组标出著名易混词；第二组列出休憩与谎言词。

entries.definition: To put something down; it needs an object, while lie does not.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物放下；需宾语，lie 不需。

entries.definition: One who tells lies.
entries.definitionCN: 说谎的人。

entries.definition: French word for place, as in in lieu of; unrelated root.
entries.definitionCN: 法语「地方」，如 in lieu of；词根无关。

entries.definition: To relax lying down or sit still.
entries.definitionCN: 躺下或静坐放松。

entries.definition: To change facts dishonestly; stronger and more official than lie.
entries.definitionCN: 不实改动事实；比 lie 更强更正式。

entries.definition: To lean back in a resting position.
entries.definitionCN: 后倚而卧。

entries.definition: A small harmless lie.
entries.definitionCN: 无伤大雅的小谎。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the two roots and the famous grammar trap.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用两个词根与著名语法陷阱。

normal.en: Posture lie: lie, lay, lain — no object needed.
normal.cn: 姿态 lie：lie、lay、lain——不需要宾语。

normal.en: Falsehood lie: lie, lied, lied — regular.
normal.cn: 谎言 lie：lie、lied、lied——规则变化。

normal.en: You lay the book (put it); you lie on the bed (rest).
normal.cn: lay 是放书，lie 是躺床。

normal.en: Idioms: lie down, lie in, white lie, lie ahead.
normal.cn: 习语：躺下、睡懒觉、善意的谎言、即将来临。

normal.en: Liar is the person; lying covers both senses as an adjective.
normal.cn: liar 是说谎者；lying 作形容词可指两种义。

abstract.en: Picture a cat stretched flat in one sunbeam.
abstract.cn: 想象一只猫摊平在阳光里。

abstract.en: Picture a map where towns rest beside rivers.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上城镇安卧河畔。

abstract.en: Picture a mask slipping off a smiling face.
abstract.cn: 想象面具从笑脸滑落。

examples.en: Lie still and the room stops spinning.
examples.cn: 躺稳别动，房间就不转了。

examples.en: He lied once and spent a year earning trust back.
examples.cn: 他说了一次谎，花了一年赢回信任。

examples.en: Adventure lies just beyond the hills.
examples.cn: 冒险就在山那边。

sensesIntro.en: Seven senses run on two separate rails: a body at rest — lying, situated, in a state, waiting ahead, buried — and a mouth astray — lying and its noun.
sensesIntro.cn: 七个义项沿两条轨道：静卧之身——躺、位于、处于、在前方等待、安葬——与失口之嘴——说谎及其名词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body laid flat; a mouth off the truth.
core.cn: 核心意象：放平的身体；偏离真相的嘴。

branches.en: THE FLAT BODY: resting now and resting forever.
branches.cn: 平放的身体：此刻安卧与永久安息。

branches.en: THE PLACE AND ITS STATE: where things lie and how they lie.
branches.cn: 位置与状态：物卧何处、处于何种状态。

branches.en: THE ROAD AHEAD: the future lies like unwalked ground.
branches.cn: 前方之路：未来如未踏之地铺展。

branches.en: THE OTHER RAIL: false words and the noun they form.
branches.cn: 另一条轨道：假话与其凝成的名词。

branches.en: THE PIVOT: stillness under both readings.
branches.cn: 轴心：两种读法共享「静止」。

intro.en: Lie has two native histories and no prefixes; the family is small and built with suffixes.

definition_zh: 生命；一生；生活；活力
definition_en: the state of being alive; the period from birth to death; the way a person lives; and the energy that makes something lively
core_image: 一株小小的绿芽从土里顶出来，把光一点点变成生长
scene: 清晨的光刚落到窗台，病床上的老人睁开眼，握住女儿的手。The nurse stayed all night to save his life.
sceneCN: 这里是「生命、性命」（第 1 个义项：活着的状态）；句意为护士守了一整夜来救他的命。图中可辨识物件：病床、输液架、窗边的光。

derivatives.zh: 由 life 加表示「没有」的后缀 -less 构成，义为「无生命的；死气沉沉的」
由 life 与 long 复合而成，义为「终身的」
由 life 的词干加 -ly 构成，义为「活泼的；有生气的」

senses.title: The state of being alive
senses.definition: the state or condition of being alive, especially for a person, animal or plant
senses.definitionCN: 活着、尚未死亡的状态，尤指人、动物或植物
senses.example: The doctor worked fast because a life was at stake.
senses.exampleCN: 医生动作很快，因为有一条命悬在那里。
senses.why: The oldest sense names the bare fact of being alive, the opposite of death, and every later use grows from that fact.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项指「活着」这个基本事实，与死亡相对，后来所有用法都从这一点生长出来。

senses.title: The span from birth to death
senses.definition: the period between birth and death, or the length of that period
senses.definitionCN: 从出生到死亡之间的整段时间，或其长度
senses.example: She spent her whole life in the same village.
senses.exampleCN: 她一辈子都住在同一个村子。
senses.why: Because being alive lasts a stretch of time, the word for life also measures that stretch, from the first breath to the last.
senses.whyCN: 因为活着会持续一段时间，表示生命的词也用来度量这一整段，从第一口气到最后一口。

senses.title: The way someone lives
senses.definition: the daily conditions, habits and activities that fill a person's existence
senses.definitionCN: 构成一个人日常存在的条件、习惯与活动
senses.example: City life suits him better than country life.
senses.exampleCN: 城市生活比乡村生活更适合他。
senses.why: Once life is a span of time, what fills that span also comes to be called life, so the word names habits and conditions rather than mere survival.
senses.whyCN: 一旦生命被看作一段时间，填满这段时间的内容也被叫作 life，于是这个词指习惯与环境，而不是仅仅活着。

senses.title: Vitality; liveliness
senses.definition: the energy or liveliness that makes a place, person or object feel alive
senses.definitionCN: 让场所、人或物显得有生气的能量与劲头
senses.example: Music brought the empty square back to life.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐让空荡的广场重新有了生气。
senses.why: The word for being alive can be moved onto things that are not alive, where it names the energy they seem to give off.
senses.whyCN: 表示「活着」的词可以移到没有生命的事物上，用来指它们散发出的那股劲。

intro.en: Life is an Old English word for being alive; it is related to the verb live and has no Latin word of the same meaning behind it.
intro.cn: life 是古英语中表示「活着」的词，与动词 live 同源，背后并没有哪个同义的拉丁词。

items.en: A reconstructed root often connected with remaining or continuing is proposed behind the Germanic family, but the reconstruction is not certain.
items.cn: 一般认为日耳曼语族背后有个表示「留下、延续」的原始印欧语词根，但这一构拟并不确定。

items.en: The Germanic noun for life and the verb for living grew up side by side from the same stock.
items.cn: 日耳曼语里表示生命的名词，与表示活着的动词，是从同一来源一起长出来的。

items.en: Old English lif named the state of being alive and could also mean the course of a person's days.
items.cn: 古英语的 lif 指活着的状态，也可指一个人一生的历程。

items.en: Middle English extended life to the way people live and to the liveliness of things, while the plural lives took its present form.
items.cn: 中古英语把 life 扩展到生活方式与事物的生气，复数 lives 也定型下来。

items.en: Modern English uses life for biology, biography, daily existence and energy, and keeps live as the related verb and adjective.
items.cn: 现代英语用 life 指生理生命、生平、日常生活与活力，并保留 live 作为相关的动词与形容词。

note.en: The first group gathers the Germanic relatives of life and its compounds; the second gathers cooler abstract words for existing.
note.cn: 第一组收 life 的日耳曼语同族词与复合词；第二组收更冷静抽象的「存在」类词。

entries.definition: To be alive, or to spend one's life in a place; the verb behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 活着，或在一地生活；名词 life 背后的动词。

entries.definition: Without life; dead or dull.
entries.definitionCN: 没有生命的；死的或沉闷的。

entries.definition: Lasting for the whole of a person's life.
entries.definitionCN: 持续一辈子的；终身的。

entries.definition: Living, not dead; the same Germanic stock as life.
entries.definitionCN: 活着的、未死的；与 life 出自同一日耳曼语源。

entries.definition: The fact of being real or present, close to but cooler than life.
entries.definitionCN: 真实存在或在场的事实，比 life 更冷静、更抽象。

entries.definition: A living creature, or the state of existing.
entries.definitionCN: 活着的生物，或存在的状态。

entries.definition: The strength and energy that make something lively.
entries.definitionCN: 让事物有生气的力量与能量。

normalIntro.en: Life and live come from one Germanic stock, and the family keeps splitting that single fact into a noun, a verb and a quality.
normalIntro.cn: life 与 live 出自同一日耳曼语源，这一族词把「活着」这一件事分成名词、动词与性质。

normal.en: Life and live come from the same Germanic stock, one as a noun and one as a verb.
normal.cn: life 与 live 出自同一日耳曼语源，一个是名词，一个是动词。

normal.en: The plural is lives with a v, because the final f of life turns voiced between vowels.
normal.cn: 复数是 lives，带 v，因为 life 词尾的 f 在两个元音之间会浊化。

normal.en: Lifeless adds -less, the suffix for absence, so it means without life.
normal.cn: lifeless 加的是表示「没有」的后缀 -less，所以意为没有生命。

normal.en: Life expectancy literally asks how long a life is expected to last.
normal.cn: life expectancy 字面上问的就是一条命预计能持续多久。

normal.en: Come to life is used of things that are not alive, such as a party or a picture.
normal.cn: come to life 常用在本来没有生命的东西上，例如聚会或画像。

abstract.en: English uses one word for the fact of being alive, the years it lasts, and the way those years are filled, because all three are one experience seen at different lengths.
abstract.cn: 英语用同一个词表示活着的事实、活着的年数以及这些年的过法，因为它们是同一段经验的不同尺度。

abstract.en: A life is both a line and a texture: it has length, and it also has a quality that can be dull or vivid.
abstract.cn: 一条命既是长度也是质感：它有长短，也有沉闷或鲜活的差别。

abstract.en: The word moves from biology to biography without blinking, which is why a person can lose a life and also live a life.
abstract.cn: 这个词从生理跨到生平毫不迟疑，所以人既可以失去一条命，也可以过一种生活。

examples.en: The doctor worked fast because a life was at stake.
examples.cn: 医生动作很快，因为有一条命悬着。

examples.en: He has lived in the same village all his life.
examples.cn: 他一辈子都住在同一个村子。

examples.en: Music brought the empty square back to life.
examples.cn: 音乐让空荡的广场重新有了生气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来福」——狗名来福，盼的就是性命平安、日子有生气；life 是生命、生活。

root: 古英语 lif（生命、活着）与动词 live 同源，一般认为其背后是日耳曼语族表示「存活、留下」的一组词；更深词源不确定，与拉丁语 vita 没有亲缘。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the fact of being alive; the senses then measure that fact as a span of years, as the way those years are lived, and as the energy they give off.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「活着」这一事实；义项随后把它量成一生的年数、看成这些年的过法，也看成它散发出的活力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small green shoot pushing up through soil and turning light into growth.
core.cn: 核心意象：一株小绿芽从土里顶出来，把光一点点变成生长。

branches.en: a heartbeat returning on a monitor
branches.cn: 监护仪上重新出现的心跳

branches.en: one person's whole stretch of years in a single village
branches.cn: 一个人在同一村子里度过的全部年岁

branches.en: a first school morning and a grandparent's fixed routine
branches.cn: 孩子上学的第一个早晨与祖辈固定的日常

branches.en: two neighbours comparing city and country habits
branches.cn: 两个邻居比较城市与乡村的习惯

branches.en: a square waking up when the band starts
branches.cn: 乐队一响，广场就醒了过来

intro.en: One Germanic noun of being alive, its verb, two English endings and two compounds that turn life into a state, a lack and a span.
intro.cn: 一个表示活着的日耳曼名词、它的动词、两个英语词尾，以及两个把 life 变成状态、缺失与跨度的复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vita means life, but it comes from a different root and is not a cognate of life.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vita 意为生命，但出自另一个词根，不是 life 的同族词。

definition_zh: 举起；抬起；提高；解除；电梯；便车
definition_en: to raise something to a higher place; to increase a level; to end a ban; and, as a noun, an elevator or a free ride
core_image: 两只手从下方托住重物，把它的重量抬离地面
scene: 楼道里的纸箱太沉，邻居伸手托住它的底部。He lifted the box onto the top shelf.
sceneCN: 这里是「举起、抬起」（第 1 个义项：把东西移到高处）；句意为他把这箱东西抬到最上层的架子上。图中可辨识物件：纸箱、货架、楼梯扶手。

derivatives.zh: 由 lift 加表示「人或物」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「举重者；升降装置」
由 lift 与 off 复合而成，义为「火箭等离地升空」
由 fork 与 lift 复合而成，义为「叉车」

senses.title: To raise something to a higher place
senses.definition: to move something upward from a lower position, usually with effort
senses.definitionCN: 把某物从较低处向上移动，通常要用些力气
senses.example: He lifted the box onto the top shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 他把箱子抬到最上层的架子上。
senses.why: The Norse verb behind lift meant to raise, and the core picture is two hands taking a weight off the ground.
senses.whyCN: lift 背后的古诺尔斯语动词本义就是举起，核心画面是两只手把重量托离地面。

senses.title: To raise a level or amount
senses.definition: to increase the level, amount or value of something
senses.definitionCN: 提高某事物的水平、数量或价值
senses.example: The new bridge lifted property prices across the river.
senses.exampleCN: 新桥抬高了河对岸的房价。
senses.why: Raising an object physically turns into raising a figure, because both move upward on an imagined scale.
senses.whyCN: 把东西举高这件事，转到数字上就成了把数字抬高，因为两者在想象的刻度上都是往上走。

senses.title: To cancel a ban or restriction
senses.definition: to end a rule, ban or order that was in force
senses.definitionCN: 结束正在实行的规定、禁令或命令
senses.example: The city lifted the night curfew last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市去年春天解除了夜间宵禁。
senses.why: A ban sits on people like a weight, so removing it is naturally described as lifting that weight off them.
senses.whyCN: 禁令像压在人们身上的重物，把它取消，自然就说成把这份重量挪开。

senses.title: An elevator
senses.definition: a machine that carries people up and down inside a building, the usual British word for an elevator
senses.definitionCN: 在楼内载人上下的机器，英式英语里常用的说法
senses.example: Take the lift to the fifth floor.
senses.exampleCN: 坐电梯到五楼。
senses.why: The noun names the device whose whole job is lifting, so the machine simply takes the name of the action.
senses.whyCN: 名词指专门负责举升的装置，于是这台机器直接取了动作的名字。

senses.title: A free ride in a vehicle
senses.definition: a ride given to someone in a car or other vehicle, usually without payment
senses.definitionCN: 让别人搭自己的车走一段，通常不收钱
senses.example: She gave me a lift to the station in the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 下雨天她顺路把我载到了车站。
senses.why: A ride lifts a person from one place to another, so an informal trip takes the same word as the upward movement.
senses.whyCN: 搭车就是把一个人从一处送到另一处，于是这段顺路的行程也用了表示上升的词。

intro.en: Lift arrived in English from Old Norse, where the verb for raising and the noun for air and height belonged together.
intro.cn: lift 从古诺尔斯语进入英语，在那里表示举起的动词与表示空气、高处的名词本是一族。

items.en: The verb lypta meant to raise or lift up, and it entered English during the Norse presence in the north of England.
items.cn: 动词 lypta 意为举起、抬升，在诺斯人活动于英格兰北部时进入英语。

items.en: The related noun lopt meant air or the sky, and it also named an upper room, which English keeps as loft.
items.cn: 同族名词 lopt 意为空气、天空，也指楼上的房间，英语保留为 loft。

items.en: Middle English lift worked as both verb and noun, covering the act of raising and the device that raises.
items.cn: 中古英语的 lift 兼作动词与名词，既指举起的动作，也指用来举升的装置。

items.en: The word took on figurative raising of prices, spirits and bans, while lift became the British word for an elevator.
items.cn: 这个词开始用于价格、情绪与禁令的抽象「抬高」，lift 也成为英式英语里「电梯」的说法。

items.en: Modern English keeps lift for raising, cancelling rules and giving rides, and uses lifting for the action itself.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 lift 表示举起、取消规定与顺路载人，并用 lifting 指举起这一动作。

note.en: The first group follows the Norse root through loft, aloft and the lift compounds; the second gathers other verbs for moving something upward.
note.cn: 第一组沿诺斯语词根收 loft、aloft 与 lift 的复合词；第二组收其他表示「往上移」的动词。

entries.definition: An upper room or a raised floor, from the same Norse word for air and height.
entries.definitionCN: 楼上的房间或架高的楼层，出自同一个表示空气与高处的诺斯词。

entries.definition: Up in the air; high above the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 在空中；高高在上。

entries.definition: A person or device that lifts.
entries.definitionCN: 举起东西的人或装置。

entries.definition: The moment a rocket or aircraft leaves the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 火箭或飞机离地的那一刻。

entries.definition: To move something to a higher position; the general verb for this action.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物移到更高处；表达这一动作的通用动词。

entries.definition: To raise to a higher level, often in a technical or formal way.
entries.definitionCN: 提升到更高水平，常带技术或正式色彩。

entries.definition: To lift something heavy with ropes or a machine.
entries.definitionCN: 用绳索或机械把重物吊起。

normalIntro.en: Lift is a Norse verb of raising whose family keeps returning to height, and whose compounds keep returning to machines and movement.
normalIntro.cn: lift 是诺斯语中表示举起的动词，词族反复回到「高处」，复合词则反复回到机械与移动。

normal.en: Lift came from a Norse verb for raising, so its oldest job is to move weight upward.
normal.cn: lift 来自诺斯语中表示举起的动词，最老的本职就是把重量往上移。

normal.en: Loft and aloft belong to the same family, which is why all three suggest height.
normal.cn: loft 与 aloft 属于同一个词族，所以它们都带着「高处」的意思。

normal.en: Lifter adds -er, the doer suffix, so it names the person or machine that lifts.
normal.cn: lifter 加的是表示执行者的后缀 -er，指举起东西的人或机器。

normal.en: Lift a ban treats a rule as a weight, and cancelling it as taking that weight away.
normal.cn: lift a ban 把规定当成压着的重物，取消就是把这重量拿走。

normal.en: Give someone a lift uses the upward motion for a short ride to a farther place.
normal.cn: give someone a lift 用「向上移动」来表示顺路载人去更远一点的地方。

abstract.en: One word covers hands, prices, bans and elevators because each is a way of moving something up or off.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时覆盖双手、价格、禁令与电梯，因为它们都是把某物往上或往外移。

abstract.en: Lift is what you do to a weight, and it is also what a building does to people all day.
abstract.cn: lift 是你对重物做的动作，也是楼房整天对人做的事。

abstract.en: The word begins with touch and ends with permission, which shows how far one simple motion can travel.
abstract.cn: 这个词从触摸开始，到许可结束，可见一个简单的动作能走多远。

examples.en: He lifted the box onto the top shelf.
examples.cn: 他把箱子抬到最上层的架子上。

examples.en: The city lifted the night curfew last spring.
examples.cn: 这座城市去年春天解除了夜间宵禁。

examples.en: She gave me a lift to the station in the rain.
examples.cn: 下雨天她顺路把我载到了车站。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「力扶特」——用力扶一把，特别能抬起来；lift 是举起。

root: 一般认为来自古诺尔斯语 lypta（举起），与 lopt（空气、高处，英语作 loft）同族；拉丁语 levare 只是意义相近，并非同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is moving weight upward; the senses then split into raising numbers, removing rules, and the machines or rides that do the lifting.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是把重量往上移；义项随后分成抬高数字、解除规定，以及替人完成举升的机器与车程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands under a heavy box, taking its weight off the floor.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手托住重箱的底部，把它的重量抬离地面。

branches.en: a box rising from floor to shelf
branches.cn: 箱子从地面升到架上

branches.en: a price line climbing after a new bridge opens
branches.cn: 新桥开通后上扬的房价曲线

branches.en: a curfew notice being taken down at night
branches.cn: 夜里被摘下的宵禁令告示

branches.en: a small metal box sliding up a shaft
branches.cn: 沿井道上升的小铁箱

branches.en: a wet passenger settling into a warm car
branches.cn: 淋湿的乘客坐进温暖的车里

intro.en: A Norse verb of raising, its noun for air and height, and the endings and compounds that turn the root into people, places and machines.
intro.cn: 一个表示举起的诺斯语动词、它表示空气与高处的名词，以及把词根变成人、地点与机器的词尾和复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin levare means to raise and gives English lever and elevation, but it is not a cognate of lift.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 levare 意为举起，英语的 lever 与 elevation 出自它，但它与 lift 并非同族。

definition_zh: 光；轻的；点燃
definition_en: brightness that lets us see, not heavy, or to set something burning
core_image: 窗边的书页被午后的光照得发亮，桌上的纸杯很轻
scene: 窗边的书页被午后的光照得发亮，桌上的纸杯很轻。Turn on the light, please.
sceneCN: 这里 light 是「光」（第 01 个义项）；句意是窗外的光把我弄醒了；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 轻轻地
轻

senses.title: Brightness that lets us see
senses.definition: Brightness that lets us see
senses.definitionCN: 让人看见的明亮
senses.example: The light from the window woke me.
senses.exampleCN: 窗外的光把我弄醒了。
senses.why: Old English leoht named brightness; the word is Germanic and related to the idea of shining.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 leoht 指明亮；这个词属日耳曼语，与「发光」的概念相关。

senses.title: Not heavy
senses.definition: Not heavy
senses.definitionCN: 分量小
senses.example: The bag is light enough to carry.
senses.exampleCN: 这个包很轻，提得动。
senses.why: The adjective light comes from a different Old English word, leoht, meaning not heavy; the two words fell together in spelling.
senses.whyCN: 形容词 light 来自另一个古英语词 leoht，意为不重；两个词后来拼写合并。

senses.title: To set something burning
senses.definition: To set something burning
senses.definitionCN: 使某物烧起来
senses.example: She lit the candle.
senses.exampleCN: 她点燃了蜡烛。
senses.why: Because light can mean a flame, the verb came to mean setting something alight.

definition_en: probable or expected; seeming suitable or promising; believable; and, as an adverb, probably
core_image: 云图上那片雨云正朝城市的方向缓缓压过来
scene: 清晨的广播里，播音员指着云图说今天午后有雨，出门的人顺手把伞塞进包里。The forecaster said it was likely to rain by noon, so she took an umbrella.
sceneCN: 这里是「很可能的」（第 1 个义项：表示某事有较大机会发生）；句意为预报员说中午前很可能下雨，于是她带上了伞。图中可辨识物件：云图、铺开的雨云带、塞进包里的折叠伞。

pos.zh: 很可能的；有希望的；合适的；可信的

senses.title: Probable or expected to happen
senses.titleCN: 很可能的；预期会发生的
senses.definition: having a high chance of happening or of being true
senses.definitionCN: 发生或属实的可能性很大
senses.example: It is likely to rain this evening.
senses.exampleCN: 今晚很可能下雨。
senses.why: The word grew out of like in the sense of having the same appearance, so something likely looks the way the expected thing looks, and that resemblance turns into probability.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从表示「长得像」的 like 长出来：一件很可能会发生的事，看起来正像预期中那件事的样子，于是「像」变成了「可能」。

senses.title: Seeming suitable or promising
senses.definition: seeming to be a good choice or to have a good chance of success
senses.definitionCN: 看起来是个好选择，或成功的机会很大
senses.example: She is the likeliest candidate for the post.
senses.exampleCN: 她是最有希望得到这个职位的人选。
senses.why: When a person looks the part, English calls that person likely, because the old sense of having the appearance of something turns into being promising.
senses.whyCN: 当一个人看起来就像那个角色，英语便说这人 likely，因为「具有某物的样子」这一旧义转成了「有希望」。

senses.title: Believable or plausible
senses.definition: seeming true or believable, often said of an excuse, an alibi or a story
senses.definitionCN: 听起来真实可信，常用于借口、不在场证明或说法
senses.example: That is a likely story, but I still do not believe it.
senses.exampleCN: 那说法倒像真的，可我还是不信。
senses.why: If something merely looks true, it can pass as true, and the ironic phrase a likely story shows exactly where appearance and credibility part company.
senses.whyCN: 一样东西只要看着像真的，就能冒充真的；反讽的「a likely story」正说明「像」与「可信」在哪儿分了家。

senses.title: Probably, as an adverb
senses.definition: used to say that something is probably true or will probably happen
senses.definitionCN: 用于表示某事大概属实或大概会发生
senses.example: They will likely agree to the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 他们大概会同意这个方案。
senses.why: The adjective ending -ly already carried the sense of manner, so the same form slid into adverb use without taking a second suffix.
senses.whyCN: 形容词词尾 -ly 本就带「以……方式」的意味，所以同一形式直接滑入副词用法，不必再加一个后缀。

intro.en: Likely began as a word for looking like something, and only later came to mean probable.
intro.cn: likely 最初表示「看起来像某物」，后来才引申为「很可能」。

items.en: A root reconstructed as līka- is generally thought to mean body or form, and from it came words for being similar in appearance.
items.cn: 一般认为有一个重构词根 līka-，意为「身体、形状」，由此产生表示「外观相似」的词。

items.en: Old English gelīc meant similar or alike, and the suffix -līc meant having the form of something.
items.cn: 古英语 gelīc 意为「相似的、相像的」，后缀 -līc 意为「具有……形状的」。

items.en: Old Norse líkligr, built from líkr and -ligr, meant likely or probable and strengthened the English word during the Norse period.
items.cn: 古诺尔斯语 líkligr 由 líkr（相像）与 -ligr 构成，意为「可能的、像样的」，在诺尔斯语影响时期强化了英语中的这个词。

items.en: Middle English used likli and likely for both a probable event and a suitable person.
items.cn: 中古英语用 likli、likely 同时表示「可能发生的事」与「合适的人」。

items.en: Modern English keeps the adjective and adds a fully accepted adverb use, especially in American writing.
items.cn: 现代英语保留形容词，并发展出被广泛接受的副词用法，尤其在美式书面语中。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the like family; the near-meaning group gathers words that measure probability.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 like 这一词族展开；近义组收表示「可能性」的词。

entries.definition: The noun for the chance that something will happen.
entries.definitionCN: 表示某事发生机会的名词：可能性。

entries.definition: Not probable or not expected to happen.
entries.definitionCN: 不太可能发生的。

entries.definition: Similar in appearance or nature.
entries.definitionCN: 外观或性质上相似的。

entries.definition: Similar to something, or to find something pleasant.
entries.definitionCN: 与……相像；喜欢。

entries.definition: Likely to happen or be true, often stronger and more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 很可能的，语气常更强也更正式。

entries.definition: Able to happen, without saying that the chance is high.
entries.definitionCN: 有可能的，但不表示机会很大。

entries.definition: Used to say what is probably true from the available evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 据现有证据推测大概如此。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on like, so every hook should connect appearance with probability.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在 like 之上，所以每条记忆钩子都该把「像」与「可能」连起来。

normal.en: Like and likely share a root: what looks like the expected thing is likely to become it.
normal.cn: like 与 likely 同根：看起来像预期结果的，很可能就会变成那个结果。

normal.en: The ending -ly marks manner and also builds adverbs, which is why likely serves as both adjective and adverb.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ly 既标记方式，又能构成副词，所以 likely 兼作形容词与副词。

normal.en: Unlikely is simply un- plus likely, and the stress stays on the first syllable of the base word.
normal.cn: unlikely 就是 un- 加 likely，重音仍落在原词的第一音节。

normal.en: Likelihood turns the adjective into a noun with -hood, the same ending seen in childhood and neighbourhood.
normal.cn: likelihood 用 -hood 把形容词变成名词，与 childhood、neighbourhood 用的是同一个后缀。

normal.en: A likely candidate looks the part, and a likely story sounds true; in both cases the eye or ear decides before the mind.
normal.cn: likely candidate 是「看着像那个人选」，a likely story 是「听着像真的」；两处都是眼睛或耳朵先于头脑作判断。

abstract.en: English first trusted the look of a thing, and then let that look become a guess about the future.
abstract.cn: 英语先相信一物的外观，再让这外观变成对未来的猜测。

abstract.en: Probability is appearance stretched over time: what resembles the usual outcome is expected to become it.
abstract.cn: 可能性就是把外观拉长时间：与常见结果相像的，就被预期会变成那个结果。

abstract.en: The same word serves a promise and a doubt, because a good appearance can raise either hope or suspicion.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能许诺也能怀疑，因为好看的外表既能让人起希望，也能让人起疑心。

examples.en: It is likely to rain this evening.
examples.cn: 今晚很可能下雨。

examples.en: She is the likeliest candidate for the post.
examples.cn: 她是最有希望得到这个职位的人选。

examples.en: They will likely agree to the plan.
examples.cn: 他们大概会同意这个方案。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来客里」——来客里有人说这单生意能成，听着很可能；likely 就是很可能。

root: 一般认为源自重构词根 līka-（身体、形状），古英语有 gelīc（相似的）与后缀 -līc，古诺尔斯语 líkligr（可能的）进一步影响英语；与 like 同族，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is looking like something; from there the senses divide into probability, suitability, credibility, and the adverb use.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「看起来像某物」；义项由此分成概率、合适、可信三种判断，以及副词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a band of rain cloud slowly pressing toward the city on a weather map.
core.cn: 核心意象：云图上那片雨云正朝城市缓缓压过来。

branches.en: a cloud band crawling toward the city
branches.cn: 一条朝城市爬来的云带

branches.en: a name at the top of a shortlist
branches.cn: 候选名单最上面的一个名字

branches.en: an excuse that sounds almost true
branches.cn: 听起来几乎是真的借口

branches.en: a sentence that starts with probably
branches.cn: 一句以「大概」开头的话

branches.en: a forecast that shapes the morning
branches.cn: 左右了清晨安排的预报

intro.en: The word is held together by the Germanic root for form and the suffix that turned similarity into probability.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「形状」的日耳曼词根，以及把相似变成可能的那个后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 限度；极限；界限；限制；限定；（口语）令人无法容忍的人或事
definition_en: the greatest amount or level allowed; a boundary; to keep something within a boundary; and, informally, an intolerable person or thing
core_image: 跑道尽头画着一条白线，越过它就算出界
scene: 操场边的公告牌写着每人每天只能领两瓶水，管理员站在桌后一瓶一瓶地数。The camp set a strict limit on drinking water during the hot week.
sceneCN: 这里是「限度、限额」（第 1 个义项：允许的最大数量）；句意为营地在炎热的一周里给饮用水定了严格限额。图中可辨识物件：公告牌、成排的水瓶、记账的纸单。

pos.zh: 限度；极限；界限；令人无法容忍的人或事

derivatives.zh: 由 limit 加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「限制；局限」
由 limit 加否定后缀 -less 构成，义为「无限制的」
由否定前缀 un- 加 limited 构成，义为「无限的；不受限制的」

senses.title: The greatest amount allowed
senses.definition: the largest amount, number or level that is allowed or possible
senses.definitionCN: 被允许或可能达到的最大数量、数目或程度
senses.example: There is a limit to how much I can carry.
senses.exampleCN: 我能搬的东西是有限度的。
senses.why: Latin limes was the path that marked the edge of a field, so a limit began as the line beyond which something stops being allowed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 limes 是标出田地边缘的小路，所以 limit 最初就是「越过就不再被允许」的那条线。

senses.title: A boundary between areas
senses.definition: a line or point marking the edge of an area, beyond which something else begins
senses.definitionCN: 标出某一区域边缘的线或点，越过之后就是别处
senses.example: The river forms the western limit of the old town.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河构成了老城的西界。
senses.why: The same boundary line can be drawn on a map as well as written into a rule, so the physical edge and the allowed amount share one word.
senses.whyCN: 同一条界线既能画在地图上，也能写进规章，所以实体边界与允许量共用一个词。

senses.title: To restrict something
senses.definition: to stop something from growing or going beyond a certain point
senses.definitionCN: 阻止某物继续增长或越过某个点
senses.example: The doctor limited his salt intake to one gram a day.
senses.exampleCN: 医生把他的盐摄入量限制在每天一克。
senses.why: Once a limit is a line, the verb is simply the act of holding things on the near side of that line.
senses.whyCN: 既然 limit 是一条线，动词就是「把事物挡在这条线的近侧」这个动作。

senses.title: An intolerable person or thing
senses.titleCN: 令人无法容忍的人或事（口语）
senses.definition: used in informal speech for a person or thing that is impossible to tolerate
senses.definitionCN: 口语中用来指让人忍无可忍的人或事
senses.example: That child is the limit; he has emptied the whole box.
senses.exampleCN: 那孩子真让人受不了，他把整盒都倒空了。
senses.why: When patience is used up, people say the behaviour has reached the limit, and the phrase then becomes a name for whoever caused it.
senses.whyCN: 耐心被耗尽时，人们说这种行为已经到了极限，这个说法于是直接用来指造成它的人。

intro.en: Limit comes straight from a Latin word for a boundary path, and it has kept the idea of a line ever since.
intro.cn: limit 直接来自一个表示「边界小路」的拉丁词，此后一直保留着「一条线」的意思。

items.en: Limes meant a boundary, a border, or the path that ran along the edge of a field.
items.cn: limes 意为边界、国界，也指标出田地边缘的那条小路。

items.en: The genitive limitis gave the stem limit-, which English kept in every form of the word.
items.cn: 属格 limitis 给出词干 limit-，英语把这个词干保留在这个词的各种形式里。

items.en: The verb limitare meant to mark out a boundary or to set bounds, and it supplied the idea of restricting.
items.cn: 动词 limitare 意为标出边界、设定范围，提供了「加以限制」这一层意思。

items.en: Middle English took limit from French and used it for a boundary or a fixed extent.
items.cn: 中古英语经法语引入 limit，用来指边界或固定的范围。

items.en: Modern English adds the everyday sense of a maximum amount and the informal sense of an intolerable person.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「最大数量」的日常义项，以及「无法容忍的人」这一口语义项。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin boundary stem; the near-meaning group gathers other words for edges and restrictions.
note.cn: 形近组沿着表示边界的拉丁词干展开；近义组收表示界线与限制的其他词。

entries.definition: A rule or condition that restricts what is possible.
entries.definitionCN: 限制可能范围的规则或条件。

entries.definition: Having no limit at all.
entries.definitionCN: 没有任何限度的。

entries.definition: Not restricted by any limit.
entries.definitionCN: 不受任何限制的。

entries.definition: To mark the boundary of something.
entries.definitionCN: 标出某物的边界。

entries.definition: A line that marks where an area ends.
entries.definitionCN: 标出区域终点的线。

entries.definition: The point at which something begins or stops.
entries.definitionCN: 某事物开始或停止的那个点。

entries.definition: An upper limit set on an amount, especially money.
entries.definitionCN: 对数量尤其是金额设定的上限。

entries.definition: A rule that limits what people may do.
entries.definitionCN: 限制人们行为的规定。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin boundary line, so every hook draws a line and then stands on one side of it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一条拉丁语的边界线，所以每条钩子都先画线，再站到线的一侧。

normal.en: Limes was a path along the edge of a field, so every limit is first a line drawn on the ground.
normal.cn: limes 是沿着田地边缘的小路，所以每个 limit 首先都是画在地上的一条线。

normal.en: The stem limit- never changes: limits, limited and limiting all keep it intact.
normal.cn: 词干 limit- 始终不变：limits、limited、limiting 都完整保留它。

normal.en: Speed limit, time limit and age limit all name the number placed on the far side of the line.
normal.cn: speed limit、time limit、age limit 都是把线另一侧的那个数字说出来。

normal.en: To limit something is to make the line do work, holding growth on the near side.
normal.cn: to limit 某物就是让这条线起作用，把增长挡在近侧。

normal.en: Limitation and limitless take opposite suffixes, -ation and -less, from the same stem.
normal.cn: limitation 与 limitless 在同一词干上加了相反的后缀 -ation 与 -less。

abstract.en: A boundary is useful only because something lies on both sides of it: the word carries the outside with it.
abstract.cn: 边界之所以有用，是因为线两边都有东西：这个词把「外面」也一起带着。

abstract.en: To set a limit is an act of trust in advance, a way of saying how far a relationship will go.
abstract.cn: 设定限度是一种事先的信任，是在说明这层关系能走多远。

abstract.en: When patience runs out, the same word that measured things turns and measures a person.
abstract.cn: 当耐心耗尽，这个原本量事物的词就转过身来量人。

examples.en: There is a limit to how much I can carry.
examples.cn: 我能搬的东西是有限度的。

examples.en: The doctor limited his salt intake to one gram a day.
examples.cn: 医生把他的盐摄入量限制在每天一克。

examples.en: The speed limit on this road is forty.
examples.cn: 这条路的限速是四十。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「厘米特」——绳子只到厘米特那么长，再多一厘米就超过限度；limit 是限度。

root: 拉丁语 limes（边界、田边小路），属格 limitis 给出词干 limit-；晚期拉丁语 limitare（划定界限）→ 法语 limite → 英语 limit；同族词多与边界、限制有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a boundary line; the senses divide into the maximum allowed, the geographical edge, the act of restricting, and the point where tolerance runs out.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「一条界线」；义项由此分为允许的最大量、地理边界、划线限制的动作，以及耐心到顶时对人的说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white line painted at the end of a running track.
core.cn: 核心意象：跑道尽头画着一条白线，越过它就算出界。

branches.cn: 写着每天两瓶的公告牌

branches.en: a river marking the edge of a town
branches.cn: 标出城镇边缘的一条河

branches.en: a doctor writing a daily maximum
branches.cn: 医生写下的每日上限

branches.cn: 空盒子和疲惫的家长

branches.cn: 跑道尽头的白线

intro.en: The word rests on a Latin noun of boundary, its genitive stem and a Late Latin verb of marking bounds.
intro.cn: 这个词依托表示边界的拉丁名词、它的属格词干，以及一个表示划界的晚期拉丁语动词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

latinEntries.meaning: to mark a boundary, to restrict

definition_zh: 限制；限度；局限；不足之处；（法律）诉讼时效；责任限额；权利或地产的限定
definition_en: a rule or condition that limits something, and a weakness or shortcoming that a method or person cannot pass
core_image: 一条画在路面上的白线，把可以走的范围圈在里面，圈外一步也不许越
scene: 论文末尾专门用一节说明样本太小、只覆盖一所学校，提醒读者结论不能推得太远。Every study states its limitations so that readers know how far the findings can travel.
sceneCN: 这里指研究自身的不足之处（第 4 个义项：局限、不足）；句意为每项研究都要说明自己的局限，读者才知道结论能走多远。场景图取象：路面上一条白线把可行范围圈住；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 限制；限度（可数或不可数）
局限；不足之处（多用复数）

derivatives.zh: 界限；限制（由拉丁语「边界」一词直接借入，兼指界线与设界之举）
有限的；受限制的（动词过去分词转形容词，指数量或范围受约束）
无限的；无边的（加表示「没有」的形容词后缀）
划定界限；划界（加表示「去除、划分」的前缀，指把边界明确画出）
限制性的（现在分词转形容词，指起约束作用）
无限的；不受限制的（加否定前缀，指没有设上限）

senses.title: The act of limiting
senses.definition: the act of keeping something within bounds, or the state of being kept within them
senses.definitionCN: 把某物保持在范围之内的动作，或受此约束的状态
senses.example: The limitation of outdoor gatherings began in October.
senses.exampleCN: 户外聚集的限制从十月开始。
senses.why: The noun comes from a Latin verb meaning to bound, so the act of drawing the line is the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词出自意为「划界」的拉丁动词，画线这个动作是最古老的义项。

senses.title: A rule that restricts
senses.definition: a rule, condition or cap that restricts what may be done, used or claimed
senses.definitionCN: 限制可以做什么、用多少或主张什么的规则、条件或上限
senses.example: The contract places a limitation on how many copies may be made.
senses.exampleCN: 合同对可以制作多少份副本设了限制。
senses.why: Once a line is drawn, people need it written down, and the written line is this sense.
senses.whyCN: 线一旦画出，人们就需要把它写下来，写下来的线就是这一义项。

senses.title: A cap on money or time
senses.definition: a fixed upper amount of money, time or resources allowed for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为某项用途所允许的金钱、时间或资源的固定上限
senses.example: There is a strict limitation on the daily water supply.
senses.exampleCN: 每日供水量有严格上限。
senses.why: Budgets and clocks are the most concrete boundaries, so the word settles there first.
senses.whyCN: 预算与时钟是最具体的边界，这个词先在这里落脚。

senses.title: A weakness of a method
senses.definition: a shortcoming in a study, method or tool that limits what its results can support
senses.definitionCN: 研究、方法或工具中的不足，限制了其结果能支撑的结论
senses.example: Every study states its limitations so that readers know how far the findings can travel.
senses.exampleCN: 每项研究都要说明自己的局限，读者才知道结论能走多远。
senses.why: Science uses the plural to admit what a design cannot see, and that candour is part of the method.
senses.whyCN: 科学用复数形式承认设计看不到的东西，这种坦白本身就是方法的一部分。

senses.title: The statute of limitations
senses.definition: the legal time limit within which a claim must be brought before it is barred
senses.definitionCN: 必须在期限之内提起诉讼、逾期即丧失胜诉权的法定时限
senses.example: The claim was dismissed because the limitation had expired.
senses.exampleCN: 由于时效已过，这项请求被驳回。
senses.why: Law puts a clock on every right, and the time limit is named after the limiting itself.
senses.whyCN: 法律给每项权利都装上时钟，这个时限就以「限制」这个动作为名。

senses.title: A cap on liability
senses.definition: a contractual maximum on the amount one party must pay for loss or damage
senses.definitionCN: 合同规定的、一方对损失或损害必须支付的最高金额
senses.example: The insurer accepted a limitation of liability of two million.
senses.exampleCN: 保险人接受了二百万的责任限额。
senses.why: Risk is made bearable by naming the worst number in advance, and the clause is named after that cap.
senses.whyCN: 事先把最坏的数字写出来，风险才可承受，这条款便以那个上限命名。

senses.title: A limit on an estate or right
senses.definition: a legal restriction on how long an estate or right may last or how it may pass
senses.definitionCN: 对某项地产或权利存续时间或转让方式的法定限定
senses.example: The deed carried a limitation on the sale of the land.
senses.exampleCN: 这份契据对土地的出售作了限定。
senses.why: Property law inherited the Roman boundary word and uses it for estates cut down to a fixed term.
senses.whyCN: 财产法继承了罗马的边界词，用它指被限定为固定期限的产权。

senses.title: A caveat in an argument
senses.definition: a qualification attached to a claim so that it is not taken too broadly
senses.definitionCN: 附加在主张之上的限定条件，使其不被过度推广
senses.example: He added a limitation: the rule holds only for small firms.
senses.exampleCN: 他加了一个限定：这条规则只适用于小公司。
senses.why: A wise claim fences its own reach, and the fence is called a limitation.
senses.whyCN: 审慎的主张会替自己围出边界，这道围栏就叫限定。

senses.title: A boundary in space
senses.definition: an outer boundary or edge, the oldest physical sense of the root
senses.definitionCN: 外部的边界或边缘，是这个词根最古老的具体含义
senses.example: The limitation of the old city wall still shows on the map.
senses.exampleCN: 旧城墙的边界在地图上仍看得出来。
senses.why: The Latin word meant a frontier between fields, and every later sense is a descendant of that ditch.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词本指田地之间的地界，后来所有义项都是那条沟的后代。

intro.en: Limitation comes from Latin limitare 'to bound', from limes, 'boundary, frontier'. The line of descent is clear; the exact date of the English noun is uncertain.
intro.cn: limitation 来自拉丁语 limitare「划界」，出自 limes「边界、前线」。词源线索清楚，这个英语名词出现的确切年代不确定。

items.en: Limes meant a boundary line, a frontier between fields or between provinces of the empire.
items.cn: limes 意为边界线，是田地之间或帝国行省之间的分界线。

items.en: The verb limitare meant to mark a boundary and, by extension, to keep something within it.
items.cn: 动词 limitare 意为标出边界，引申为把某物留在边界之内。

items.en: Limitio and limitatio named the marking of a bound, a word of surveyors and lawyers.
items.cn: limitio 与 limitatio 指划定边界，是测量员与法律人的用语。

items.en: The noun entered English in the fifteenth century through legal and scholarly French; the exact date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个名词在十五世纪经由法律与学术法语进入英语；确切年代不确定。

items.en: Modern English split the word two ways: the limitations of a study, and the limitation of liability in a contract.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词分成两支：研究的局限，以及合同中的责任限额。

items.en: The statute of limitations gave the word a clock, naming the period beyond which a right cannot be pursued.
items.cn: 诉讼时效法规给这个词装上了时钟，指超过之后权利便无法追索的期间。

note.en: The first group shares the boundary root or looks close; the second group holds the words that often stand in for limitation in argument and in law.
note.cn: 第一组或共享「边界」词根，或字形相近；第二组是论证与法律中常替代「限制、局限」的词。

entries.definition: The plain noun and verb for a boundary or a cap.
entries.definitionCN: 最朴素的边界或上限名词，也可作动词。

entries.definition: Restricted in amount or scope, the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 在数量或范围上受限制的形容词。

entries.definition: The drawing of a boundary, especially between states or fields.
entries.definitionCN: 划定边界，尤指国界或领域之间。

entries.definition: To remove something; it looks like the same family but comes from limen, a threshold.
entries.definitionCN: 清除某物；看似同族，其实出自意为「门槛」的 limen。

entries.definition: Occupying a threshold or in-between state, from limen rather than limes.
entries.definitionCN: 处于门槛或过渡状态，出自 limen 而非 limes。

entries.definition: A rule that prevents something, often imposed by authority.
entries.definitionCN: 阻止某事的规则，通常由权威施加。

entries.definition: A factor that forces a choice, close to limitation in research writing.
entries.definitionCN: 迫使作出选择的因素，在研究写作中接近「局限」。

entries.definition: A failure to reach a standard, the plain word for a weakness.
entries.definitionCN: 未能达到标准，是最朴素的「缺点」说法。

entries.definition: A disadvantage that makes something less attractive.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物吸引力下降的不利之处。

entries.definition: A warning or condition attached to a claim or permission.
entries.definitionCN: 附在主张或许可之上的警告或条件。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real frontier word, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「边界」词、真实同族词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Limes meant the frontier of the empire, so a limitation is a line drawn at the edge of what is allowed.
normal.cn: limes 指帝国的前线，限制就是画在允许范围边缘的一条线。

normal.en: The family runs limit, limited, limitless and delimitation.
normal.cn: 同族词有 limit、limited、limitless 与 delimitation。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: limitations of the study, time limitation, limitation of liability.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出用法：研究的局限、时间限制、责任限额。

normal.en: In law the plural has a life of its own: the statute of limitations.
normal.cn: 在法律里复数形式自成一体：诉讼时效。

normal.en: Eliminate and liminal are false friends; they come from limen, a threshold.
normal.cn: eliminate 与 liminal 是假朋友，它们出自意为门槛的 limen。

abstract.en: A limitation honestly stated is a gift to the reader, not a weakness of the writer.
abstract.cn: 老实说出的局限是给读者的礼物，而不是作者的无能。

abstract.en: Every boundary that keeps something in also keeps something out.
abstract.cn: 每道把东西圈进来的边界，也把另一些东西关在外面。

abstract.en: The line that protects also instructs; it tells you where the work begins.
abstract.cn: 起保护作用的线同时在指路，它告诉你工作从哪里开始。

examples.en: The report lists three limitations of its own method.
examples.cn: 报告列出自身方法的三处局限。

examples.en: A limitation on imports raised the price of steel.
examples.cn: 进口限制抬高了钢材价格。

examples.en: The suit was filed within the limitation period.
examples.cn: 诉讼是在时效期间内提起的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「利米泰申」——地上画一条白线，线外不许走：限制、局限

root: 拉丁语 limitare「划界」← limes「边界、前线」；经法律与学术法语于十五世纪进入英语。同族有 limit、limited、delimitation；eliminate 与 liminal 出自 limen「门槛」，属形近不同源。名词进入英语的确切年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all descend from one boundary: the act of bounding, a restricting rule, a cap on money or time, a weakness of method, the statute of limitations, a liability cap, a limit on an estate, a caveat in argument, and a boundary in space.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都出自同一条边界：划界之举、限制性规定、金额或时间的上限、方法的局限、诉讼时效、责任限额、对地产或权利的限定、论证中的保留，以及空间上的边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white line painted across a road, with everything beyond it out of bounds.
core.cn: 核心意象：路面上画着一条白线，线外一切都不得越过。

branches.en: THE LINE ITSELF: a frontier drawn in space, and the act of drawing it.
branches.cn: 线本身：在空间里画出的边界，以及画线的动作。

branches.en: THE WRITTEN CAP: a rule or a fixed amount of money, time or water that may not be exceeded.
branches.cn: 写下来的上限：不可超过的规则，或金钱、时间、用水的定额。

branches.en: THE HONEST WEAKNESS: what a method cannot see, and the caveat that keeps a claim from spreading too far.
branches.cn: 诚实的弱点：方法看不到的东西，以及防止主张过度扩张的保留。

branches.en: THE LEGAL CLOCK AND DEED: a period after which a right is barred, and a term fixed on an estate.
branches.cn: 法律的时钟与契据：过期即失权的期间，以及为地产设定的期限。

branches.en: THE LIABILITY CAP: the worst number named in advance so that risk can be borne.
branches.cn: 责任限额：事先写出的最坏数字，好让风险可以承担。

intro.en: Limitation is a Latin boundary word turned into an abstract noun, with a family that runs through law and science.
intro.cn: limitation 是把一个拉丁边界词变成抽象名词，其词族贯穿法律与科学。

latinIntro.en: Limes and limitare are the sources; the noun ending came through Latin limitatio.
latinIntro.cn: limes 与 limitare 是来源，名词词尾经由拉丁语 limitatio 而来。

items.meaning: a marking of bounds; a restriction
items.example: The noun covers a rule, a weakness and a legal period.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词兼指规定、弱点与法定期间。

items.example: It named the edge of a field or of an empire.
items.exampleCN: 它指田地或帝国的边缘。

items.meaning: to bound, to mark a limit
items.example: The verb supplies the action behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供名词背后的动作。

items.example: It builds limitation, demarcation and estimation.
items.exampleCN: 它构成限制、划界与估计等词。

items.example: The short form is both noun and verb.
items.exampleCN: 短形既可作名词也可作动词。

items.example: The participle became the everyday adjective.
items.exampleCN: 过去分词成了日常形容词。

items.example: It builds limitless, the opposite of limited.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 limitless，即 limited 的反面。

items.example: It builds delimitation, the drawing of a border.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 delimitation，即划定边界。

items.example: It builds limiting, as in a limiting factor.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 limiting，如限制因素。

latinEntries.example: Latin limes means boundary or frontier.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 limes 意为边界、前线。

latinEntries.example: Medieval Latin limitare means to mark a boundary.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 中世纪拉丁语 limitare 意为划定边界。

latinEntries.example: Latin limitatio means a marking of bounds.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 limitatio 意为划定界限。

definition_zh: 线；线条；排；队；线路；铁路线；一行字；台词
definition_en: a long thin mark drawn on a surface, a row of people or things, a route or railway track, a row of written words, or the words an actor speaks
core_image: 一根细线在纸面上被拉直，留下一道笔直的灰痕
scene: 雨停后，操场上还留着一条浅浅的白线，孩子们沿着它站成一排。The teacher told the class to stand in a line before the race.
sceneCN: 这里 line 是「排、队」（第 2 个义项：人排成的一列）；句意为老师让全班在比赛前排成一排。图中可辨识物件：浅浅的白线、塑胶跑道、站成一列的孩子。

derivatives.zh: 由 line 加 -ar 构成，义为「直线的；线性的」
经古法语 ligne 进入英语，义为「世系；血统」，指一脉相承的线
由 line 加 -ing 构成，义为「衬里；内层」，指贴在内侧的一层
由 line 与 up 复合，义为「阵容；排好的一队人」

senses.title: A long thin mark on a surface
senses.definition: a long narrow mark left on a surface, especially one drawn or printed straight
senses.definitionCN: 留在表面上的细长痕迹，尤指画得或印得笔直的痕迹
senses.example: Draw a straight line from the dot to the edge.
senses.exampleCN: 从那个点画一条直线到边缘。
senses.why: Latin linea first named a thread of linen, and a thread pulled tight is the oldest straight edge; the mark left on paper inherited the name of the thread.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 linea 本指一根亚麻线，而把线拉紧正是最古老的直边；纸上留下的痕迹便继承了这根线的名字。

senses.title: A row of people or things waiting
senses.definition: a row of people or things standing one behind another, especially while waiting for something
senses.definitionCN: 人或物一个接一个排成的一列，尤指等候某事时形成的队伍
senses.example: We stood in line for an hour to get tickets.
senses.exampleCN: 我们排了一个小时的队才买到票。
senses.why: A drawn line and a queue have the same outline, one long narrow strip; English lets the visible stripe stand for the people standing along it.
senses.whyCN: 画出的线和排队的人群轮廓相同，都是一条细长的带子；英语便让这条看得见的带子代替站在上面的人。

senses.title: A route or a track for transport
senses.definition: a route along which buses, trains or other transport run, or a set of rails laid for trains
senses.definitionCN: 公共汽车、火车等运行的路线，或为火车铺设的轨道
senses.example: The new line will connect the airport with the city centre.
senses.exampleCN: 这条新线路将把机场与市中心连接起来。
senses.why: A route becomes a line the moment it is drawn on a map, and transport planners still speak of opening a line; the map stroke turned into the thing travellers ride.
senses.whyCN: 一条路线画上地图的那一刻就成了「线」，交通规划者至今也说「开一条线」；地图上的一笔于是变成了乘客乘坐的东西。

senses.title: A row of written words
senses.definition: a row of written or printed words, especially one verse of a poem or one entry in a list
senses.definitionCN: 书写或印刷出来的一行字，尤指诗的一行或清单中的一项
senses.example: The first line of the poem is repeated at the end.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗的第一行在结尾处重复出现。
senses.why: Printing sets words in a narrow horizontal band, and that band repeats the shape of a drawn stroke; the row of type took over the same name.
senses.whyCN: 印刷把文字排进一条窄窄的水平带，这条带子和画出的一笔形状相同；于是一行铅字也用了同一个名字。

senses.title: Words spoken by an actor
senses.definition: one of the sentences that an actor has to speak in a play or film
senses.definitionCN: 演员在戏剧或电影中要说的一句或几句词
senses.example: She forgot her line in the second act.
senses.exampleCN: 她在第二幕忘了自己的台词。
senses.why: A script is set out row by row, each row assigned to a character; the written row became the actor's unit of speech, so the page's line turned into the stage's line.
senses.whyCN: 剧本是一行一行写成的，每一行分给一个角色；纸上的一行于是成了演员说话的单位，页面上的一行就变成了台上的一句台词。

intro.en: Line comes from a Latin word for a linen thread, and that thread is the physical model behind every later sense.
intro.cn: line 来自拉丁语中表示「亚麻线」的词，而这根线正是后来每个义项背后的实物模型。

items.en: Linum named the flax plant and the cloth woven from it; Greek linon is the older form of the same word.
items.cn: linum 指亚麻这种植物，也指用它织成的布；希腊语 linon 是同一个词更早的形式。

items.en: A linea was a thread of linen and then any cord; stretched between two points, it also marked a boundary or a straight edge.
items.cn: linea 本是一根亚麻线，后来泛指绳子；在两点之间拉紧时，它还能标出边界或直边。

items.en: The verb lineare meant to make something straight or to set it in a line, and linearis described whatever belongs to a line.
items.cn: 动词 lineare 意为使某物变直或排成一线，形容词 linearis 则描述与线有关的东西。

items.en: Old French ligne carried the senses of a line, a row and a line of descent, and English borrowed it after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语的 ligne 兼指线、行以及一脉相承的世系，英语在诺曼时期之后把它借了过来。

items.en: Modern English keeps the drawn mark and adds the queue, the railway route, the verse row, the actor's speech and a whole field of work.
items.cn: 现代英语保留画出的痕迹，又加上队列、铁路线路、诗行、演员的台词，以及某一个行业。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin thread of linen; the near-meaning group gathers words for rows, routes and borders.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「亚麻线」之上的词；近义组收表示行、路线与边界的词。

entries.definition: To put things into a straight line, from French a ligne, literally into line.
entries.definitionCN: 使排成直线；来自法语 a ligne，字面就是「成线」，与 line 同源。

entries.definition: A line of descent from an ancestor.
entries.definitionCN: 世系；血统；沿用古法语 ligne 中「一脉相承的线」这一用法。

entries.definition: Arranged in a line or relating to lines.
entries.definitionCN: 排成直线的；与线有关的；由 line 加 -ar 构成。

entries.definition: Cloth woven from flax.
entries.definitionCN: 亚麻布；与 line 同出拉丁语 linum（亚麻）。

entries.definition: A number of things arranged side by side.
entries.definitionCN: 一排；一行，横向并排的一列东西。

entries.definition: A line of people waiting for something, the usual British word.
entries.definitionCN: 排队等候的队伍，英式常用说法。

entries.definition: The way from one place to another.
entries.definitionCN: 路线；从一处到另一处的路径。

entries.definition: The line that marks the edge of an area.
entries.definitionCN: 边界；标出一个区域边缘的线。

normalIntro.en: The word starts as a thread of linen, and every branch keeps the shape of one long narrow strip.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词最初是一根亚麻线，后来每个分支都保留着一条细长带子的形状。

normal.en: Latin linea is a linen thread and linum is the flax plant that makes it, so the word is a string before it is a mark.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 linea 是一根亚麻线，linum 是织出它的亚麻；所以这个词先是绳子，后来才是痕迹。

normal.en: A mason stretches a cord between two pegs to keep a wall straight, which is why a drawn mark and a boundary share one word.
normal.cn: 泥瓦匠在两个木桩之间拉紧一根绳来把墙砌直，画出的痕迹与边界因此共用一个词。

normal.en: On a map every railway is a single stroke, so a company calls its route a line.
normal.cn: 在地图上每条铁路都是一笔，所以铁路公司把自己的路线叫作 line。

normal.en: A poem is printed in rows, and an actor is handed one row at a time; the written row and the spoken line are the same shape.
normal.cn: 诗是一行一行印出来的，演员也一次拿到一行；纸上的一行和口中的一句形状相同。

normal.en: Americans stand in line while the British stand in a queue; both describe one narrow strip of waiting people.
normal.cn: 美国人说 stand in line，英国人说 stand in a queue，两种说法都是在描述一条细长的等候队伍。

abstract.en: One word for thread, mark, queue, rail and speech suggests English trusts a single shape to hold very different things.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时表示线、痕迹、队列、铁轨和台词，说明英语相信一种形状就能装下很不一样的东西。

abstract.en: A line both joins and separates: it connects two points and it divides two fields.
abstract.cn: 线既能连接也能分隔：它把两点连起来，也把两片田地分开。

abstract.en: Reading a script row by row is a reminder that a play exists first as lines on paper.
abstract.cn: 一行一行读剧本会让人想起：一出戏最初只是纸上的一行行字。

examples.cn: 从那个点画一条直线到边缘。

examples.en: We stood in line for an hour to get tickets.
examples.cn: 我们排了一个小时的队才买到票。

examples.en: She forgot her line in the second act.
examples.cn: 她在第二幕忘了自己的台词。

root: 拉丁语 linum（亚麻）→ linea（亚麻线、线、界线）→ 古法语 ligne → 英语 line；同族词多与线、排列、连续的血脉有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core image is a taut thread; from it flow the drawn mark, the queue, the route on a map, the printed row and the actor's speech.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心意象是一根拉紧的线；由此分出画出的痕迹、排队的人群、地图上的路线、印刷的一行字和演员的台词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a taut thread laid across paper, leaving one straight grey mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根拉紧的线横过纸面，留下一道笔直的灰痕。

branches.en: a pencil drawing a ruled line across the page
branches.cn: 铅笔在纸上画出一道笔直的线

branches.en: a map with one long stroke joining two towns
branches.cn: 地图上一条长线连起两个城镇

branches.en: a queue curling past the ticket window
branches.cn: 排队的人绕过了售票窗口

branches.cn: 一首诗排成整齐的诗行

branches.en: an actor waiting for a cue backstage
branches.cn: 演员在后台等提示

intro.en: A Latin word for flax, its thread and its verb, a French reshaping and two English suffixes carry line from string to mark, route and speech.
intro.cn: 一个表示亚麻的拉丁词、它的「线」和动词形式、一次法语改写，再加两个英语后缀，把 line 从绳子一路带到痕迹、路线与台词。

latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 链环；连接物；纽带；连接；关联；链接
definition_en: one ring of a chain; something that joins two things; to connect or associate people, objects, or ideas
core_image: 两段铁链由中间一个环扣住，环环相扣，力量沿链条传递
scene: 铁路调度室里，调度员把两个货运站接进同一条新支线。He used the panel to link the two freight yards to the new branch line, and a green line appeared between the two dots.
sceneCN: 这里 link 是「把两点连成一条线路」（第 6 个义项：交通连线）；句意：他用调度台把两个货运站连到新支线上，屏幕上两点之间多出一条绿线。图中可辨识物件：铁路线路图、两个货运站标记、新支线绿线、调度台；对应第 1 个义项。
