senses.title: Chain ring: one loop in a chain
senses.definition: a single ring of metal that forms one unit of a chain
senses.definitionCN: 构成链条一个单元的单个金属环
senses.example: One link of the chain had rusted through.
senses.exampleCN: 链条上有一个环已经锈穿了。
senses.why: The earliest English sense is the physical ring. Everything else grows from this object: a chain is a row of rings, and each ring holds the next.
senses.whyCN: 英语最早的义项就是这种实体环。其余义项都从这一物件生长出来：链条是一排环，而每个环都扣住下一个。

senses.title: Connector: a piece that joins two ends
senses.titleCN: 连接件：把两端扣在一起的部件
senses.definition: a physical part or device that fastens two separate parts together
senses.definitionCN: 把两个分离部件扣合在一起的实体部件或装置
senses.example: A steel link joined the two sections of the fence.
senses.exampleCN: 一个钢制连接件把围栏的两段接了起来。
senses.why: A chain ring already does the work of holding two neighbours. The word is therefore ready to name any small piece whose job is to join two ends.
senses.whyCN: 链环本来就在承担“扣住左右两环”的工作。因此这个词很自然地可以指任何以“接合两端”为职责的小部件。

senses.title: Bond between people or groups
senses.titleCN: 纽带：人与人、群体与群体之间的联结
senses.definition: a relationship or connection between people, groups, or organizations
senses.definitionCN: 人与人、群体或组织之间的关系或联结
senses.example: The exchange programme created a lasting link between the two schools.
senses.exampleCN: 交换项目在两所学校之间建立了持久的纽带。
senses.why: Move from metal to society: the ring that held two chain ends now holds two people or institutions. The connection is no longer visible, but it still constrains and carries.
senses.whyCN: 从金属转向社会：原本扣住两节链子的环，现在扣住两个人或两个机构。联结不再可见，但仍在约束与传递。

senses.title: Join physically: connect two things
senses.titleCN: 实体连接：把两件东西接起来
senses.definition: to connect two objects or places so that they are joined or can work together
senses.definitionCN: 把两个物体或地点连接起来，使其接合或能协同运作
senses.example: Workers linked the new pipe to the old water main.
senses.exampleCN: 工人把新管道接到旧的总水管上。
senses.why: The noun turns into a verb: to link is to act as the ring, putting oneself or a part between two ends and holding them together.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词：link 就是充当那个环，把自己或某个部件放在两端之间，把它们扣住。

senses.title: Associate ideas or evidence
senses.titleCN: 关联：把观念、证据或因果串起来
senses.definition: to show or establish a connection between ideas, facts, or causes
senses.definitionCN: 表明或建立观念、事实或原因之间的联系
senses.example: The study links long commutes to higher stress levels.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究把长途通勤与更高的压力水平联系起来。
senses.why: A chain of reasoning is also a row of rings: each claim holds the next. To link two facts is to insert the ring that makes them one sequence rather than two isolated items.
senses.whyCN: 推理链同样是一排环：每个论断扣住下一个。把两个事实 link 起来，就是插入那个让它们成为一条序列、而非两个孤立项的环。

senses.title: Transport connection: a route between two points
senses.titleCN: 交通连线：连接两点的线路
senses.definition: a transport route or service that connects two places
senses.definitionCN: 连接两地的交通路线或运输服务
senses.example: The new rail link cuts the journey to forty minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 新的铁路连线把行程缩短到四十分钟。
senses.why: Two stations are like two chain ends; the rail line is the ring that joins them into one network. The image scales from a hand-held chain to a map.
senses.whyCN: 两个车站就像链条的两端，铁路线则是把二者接入同一网络的环。这个意象从手中的链条放大到地图上。

senses.title: Digital link: hyperlink or network connection
senses.titleCN: 数字链接：超链接或网络连接
senses.definition: a hyperlink in a document, or a connection between computers or network nodes
senses.definitionCN: 文档中的超链接，或计算机、网络节点之间的连接
senses.example: Click the link to open the full report.
senses.exampleCN: 点击链接打开完整报告。
senses.why: A webpage is a node and a hyperlink is the ring that carries a reader from one page to another. The same join-and-carry structure is now made of protocol rather than metal.
senses.whyCN: 网页是一个节点，超链接则是把读者从一页带到另一页的环。同样的“接合与传递”结构，如今由协议而不是金属构成。

senses.title: Link arms: join bodies in contact
senses.definition: to join arms or hands with someone, especially as a sign of closeness or support
senses.definitionCN: 与某人挽臂或牵手，尤表示亲近或相互支持
senses.example: The two friends linked arms and walked into the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 两个朋友挽着手臂走进大厅。
senses.why: Here the human body supplies both ends: bent arms form the rings. The verb returns to its most concrete physical action while keeping the idea of mutual holding.
senses.whyCN: 这里两端都由人体提供：弯起的手臂就是环。动词回到最具体的身体动作，同时保留“相互扣住”的意思。

senses.title: Missing link: the absent ring in a sequence
senses.titleCN: 缺环：序列中缺失的一环
senses.definition: in the phrase missing link, the absent piece needed to complete an evolutionary or logical chain
senses.definitionCN: 用于 missing link，指完成演化链或论证链所缺的那一环
senses.example: The fossil was hailed as the missing link between the two species.
senses.exampleCN: 这块化石被誉为两个物种之间缺失的一环。
senses.why: If a chain is only as strong as its rings, one absent ring breaks the sequence. The phrase turns a physical gap into a metaphor for an unexplained step.
senses.whyCN: 如果链条的强度取决于每一环，那么缺一个环就断了整条序列。这个短语把实体缺口变成了“无法解释的中间步骤”的隐喻。

senses.title: Link up: separate parts meet and join
senses.titleCN: 汇合：分开的部分相遇并联结
senses.definition: in the phrasal verb link up, to join or meet after being separate
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语动词 link up，表示原本分开的部分连接或会合
senses.example: The two rescue teams linked up at the tunnel entrance.
senses.exampleCN: 两支救援队在隧道口会合了。
senses.why: The particle up adds completion: the ring is not merely placed but closed. Separate parties become one continuous chain, which is why the phrase suits meetings and mergers.
senses.whyCN: 小品词 up 补充“完成”：环不只是放上去，而是扣合封闭。分开的各方变成一条连续的链，因此这个短语适合会合与合并。

intro.en: Link was borrowed from Old Norse, not inherited from Old English. The chain-ring sense is solid; the jump to a bend root in Indo-European is generally believed rather than proved.
intro.cn: link 是从古诺斯语借入的，而不是从古英语继承的。链环义很确定；上溯到印欧语“弯曲”词根则属于一般认为是，而非已经证明。

items.en: The noun probably comes from Old Norse hlekkr 'link of a chain', with a related verb hlekkja 'to chain'. Old Norse gave English many everyday words during the Viking period.
items.cn: 名词很可能来自古诺斯语 hlekkr“链环”，并有相关动词 hlekkja“用链子拴住”。维京时期古诺斯语给英语带来了大量日常词。

items.en: The Norse word is traced to Proto-Germanic *hlankiz, a formation from a root meaning 'to bend'. A ring is metal bent back on itself.
items.cn: 这个诺斯语词可追溯到原始日耳曼语 *hlankiz，由表示“弯曲”的词根构成。环就是金属弯回自身形成的形状。

items.en: The deeper source is generally believed to be PIE *kleng- 'to bend, turn'. The same family is often linked to angle and other bend words, but the reconstruction is not certain.
items.cn: 更深的来源一般认为是原始印欧语 *kleng-“弯曲、转折”。同一词族常被与 angle 等“弯折”词联系起来，但这一重构并不确定。

items.en: English records the noun in the early 15c. and the verb in the late 14c., first in the literal sense of fitting with chain links.
items.cn: 英语中名词最早记录于 15 世纪早期，动词记录于 14 世纪晚期，最初都是“装上链环”的字面义。

items.en: From a metal ring the word extends to any connection: rail links, personal links, links between facts, and finally hyperlinks. The chain image survives in missing link and weakest link.
items.cn: 从金属环出发，这个词扩展到任何连接：铁路连线、人际纽带、事实之间的关联，最后是超链接。链条意象仍活在 missing link 与 weakest link 中。

note.en: The first group tests spelling and derivation around link; the second separates four kinds of connection by strength, direction, and domain.
note.cn: 第一组检查 link 周围的拼写与派生关系；第二组按强度、方向和领域区分四种“连接”。

entries.definition: the act or system of linking; a mechanical or genetic connection. It is link plus the noun suffix -age.
entries.definitionCN: 连接行为或连接系统；机械或遗传上的联动。它是 link 加名词后缀 -age。

entries.definition: to shut and open the eyes quickly. It rhymes and looks close but has a different, uncertain origin.
entries.definitionCN: 快速眨眼。它押韵、词形接近，但来源不同且不确定。

entries.definition: coloured liquid used for writing or printing. It shares the -ink ending only; there is no link in it.
entries.definitionCN: 用于书写或印刷的彩色液体。它只共享 -ink 结尾，与 link 没有词源关系。

entries.definition: to join two things so that they touch or work together. It is the broad neutral verb, while link often suggests a chain-like intermediate part.
entries.definitionCN: 把两物接合，使其接触或协同运作。它是最宽泛中性的动词，而 link 常暗示有一个链环式的中间部件。

entries.definition: to fasten one thing to another, usually a smaller thing to a larger one. It stresses physical fixing, not mutual relationship.
entries.definitionCN: 把一物固定到另一物上，通常是小物附于大物。它强调实体固定，而不是相互关联。

entries.definition: to tie or fasten tightly, or to place under a moral or legal obligation. It is stronger and more restrictive than link.
entries.definitionCN: 紧紧捆扎或固定，或使承担道德、法律义务。它比 link 更强、更具约束力。

entries.definition: the way two people or groups are connected and behave toward each other. It names the durable social tie that link describes.
entries.definitionCN: 两个人或群体相互连接与相处的方式。它命名了 link 所描述的那种持久社会纽带。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the physical chain ring, the fixed phrases missing link and weakest link, and the modern hyperlink.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：实体的链环、固定短语 missing link 与 weakest link，以及现代的超链接。

normal.en: A chain is a row of rings; one ring is a link. Take one out and the chain falls apart.
normal.cn: 链条是一排环，一个环就是一个 link。取走一个，整条链就散了。

normal.en: The weakest link is the ring that breaks first, so the phrase means the most vulnerable part of any system.
normal.cn: weakest link 是最先断的那个环，因此这个短语指任何系统中最脆弱的部分。

normal.en: The missing link is the ring absent from a sequence, especially an evolutionary chain.
normal.cn: missing link 是序列中缺失的那个环，尤指演化链上的缺环。

normal.en: Link up means the ring is finally closed: two separate parties meet and become one chain.
normal.cn: link up 表示环终于扣合：两个分开的方会合，变成一条链。

normal.en: A hyperlink does the same job on the web: one click carries you from one page to the next.
normal.cn: 超链接在网络上做同一件事：一次点击把你从一页带到下一页。

abstract.en: Two islands with a bridge between them: the bridge is not either island, yet without it they are separate worlds.
abstract.cn: 两座岛之间有一座桥：桥不属于任何一座岛，但没有它，两座岛就是分开的世界。

abstract.en: A chain has no centre: every ring holds the next and is held by the previous, so the link is a position rather than a thing.
abstract.cn: 链条没有中心：每个环都扣住下一个，又被上一个扣住，因此“环”是一种位置，而不是一个孤立物件。

abstract.en: A web of nodes and edges: the nodes are what we see, the links are the invisible lines along which influence travels.
abstract.cn: 由节点和边构成的网：节点是我们看得见的东西，链接则是影响沿之传递的看不见的线。

examples.en: The bridge links the island to the mainland.
examples.cn: 这座桥把海岛与大陆连接起来。

examples.en: Researchers have found a link between sleep loss and poor memory.
examples.cn: 研究者发现睡眠不足与记忆力差之间存在关联。

examples.en: Send me the link to the recording when it is ready.
examples.cn: 录音准备好后把链接发给我。

dict_mnemonic.text: “林克”——游戏主角林克把地图上的各个地点串起来 → link 连接

root: 古诺斯语 hlekkr“链环”，原始日耳曼语 *hlankiz；核心是“一环扣一环”，引申为任何连接、纽带与关联。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of link, all built on one object: a ring that holds two ends together. The ring becomes a connector, a human bond, a route, a hyperlink, a missing step, and finally the act of closing the chain.
sensesIntro.cn: link 的十个义项都建立在一个物件上：把两端扣住的环。这个环变成连接件、人际纽带、线路、超链接、缺失的步骤，最后变成“把链扣合”的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one ring holds the ring before it and the ring after it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个环同时扣住前一个环与后一个环。

branches.en: PHYSICAL RING: the literal chain link and any part that fastens two ends.
branches.cn: 实体环：字面的链环，以及任何接合两端的部件。

branches.en: HUMAN CONTACT: the ring becomes a bond between people or a joining of arms.
branches.cn: 人际接触：环变成人与人之间的纽带，或手臂的相互扣住。

branches.en: INFRASTRUCTURE: pipes, rails and routes are rings that join places into a network.
branches.cn: 基础设施：管道、铁路与航线都是把地点接入网络的环。

branches.en: LOGICAL CHAIN: facts are linked like rings, and a missing ring explains why a sequence fails.
branches.cn: 逻辑链：事实像环一样被串起，缺环则解释了序列为何断裂。

branches.en: DIGITAL AND COMPLETION: a hyperlink carries a reader, and link up closes the ring.
branches.cn: 数字与完成：超链接把读者带过去，link up 则把环扣合封闭。

intro.en: Link is a borrowed Germanic noun and verb, not a prefixed Latin word. English adds -age, -ed, -er and -ing to build its family.
intro.cn: link 是借入的日耳曼语名词兼动词，不是带前缀的拉丁词。英语通过 -age、-ed、-er、-ing 构成它的词族。

latinIntro.en: Link has no Latin ancestor. If the Indo-European bend root *kleng- is correct, it is a distant cousin of angle, ankle and anchor, but that link is generally believed rather than established.
latinIntro.cn: link 没有拉丁语祖先。如果印欧语“弯曲”词根 *kleng- 成立，它与 angle、ankle、anchor 是远亲，但这一联系只是一般认为，并未确立。

items.meaning: the act or system of linking; a mechanical or genetic connection
items.meaningCN: 连接；联系；联动机制（-age 构成行为或系统名词）
items.example: The linkage between the two levers controls the brake.
items.exampleCN: 两根杠杆之间的联动机构控制刹车。

items.meaningCN: 相连的；有关联的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.example: The two problems are closely linked.

items.meaning: a program or device that joins separate pieces
items.meaningCN: 连接程序；链接器（-er 表示执行该动作的物）
items.example: The linker combines the object files into one program.
items.exampleCN: 链接器把多个目标文件合并成一个程序。

items.meaning: the act of connecting; serving to connect
items.meaningCN: 连接；起连接作用的（-ing 构成动作或功能词）
items.example: A linking verb joins a subject to its description.
items.exampleCN: 连系动词把主语与其描述连接起来。

items.example: It forms linkage, a set of connections.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 linkage，即一组连接。

items.example: You can unlink the file from the message.
items.exampleCN: 你可以把文件从消息里解除链接。

items.meaning: a clickable cross-reference on a page
items.example: Click the hyperlink to open the source.

items.meaning: a joining of two systems or groups
items.example: The rail link-up took ten years to complete.
items.exampleCN: 这条铁路的接轨花了十年才完成。

latinEntries.meaning: a corner or the space between two lines
latinEntries.meaningCN: 角；两条线之间的空间（与“弯曲”词根有远亲关系）

latinEntries.structure: Old English ancleow, from PIE *ang- (to bend)
latinEntries.meaning: the joint where the foot bends
a heavy device that holds a ship in place
latinEntries.meaningCN: 锚；把船固定住的重物（原义与“弯钩”有关）
三角形；有三个角的平面图形

definition_zh: 嘴唇；边缘；口沿；不逊的话；（兰花的）唇瓣
definition_en: either of the two soft edges of the mouth, the rim of an opening, rude talk, or the lower petal of an orchid
core_image: 两片柔软的唇轻轻合拢，嘴角压成一条浅浅的缝
scene: 冬天的风把孩子的嘴唇吹得发红，他忍不住舔了舔。The cold wind left her lips dry and cracked.
sceneCN: 这里 lip 是「嘴唇」（第 1 个义项：嘴的两片软边）；句意为冷风把她的嘴唇吹得又干又裂。图中可辨识物件：冻红的脸、干裂的嘴角、竖起的衣领。

pos.zh: 嘴唇；边缘；口沿；不逊的话；（兰花的）唇瓣

derivatives.zh: 由 lip 加 -y 构成，义为「爱顶嘴的；无礼的」，多用于英式口语
由 lip 与 stick 复合，义为「口红」
由 lip 与 read 复合，义为「看口型读懂话」
由 lip 与 sync 复合，义为「对口型假唱」

senses.title: Either of the two soft edges of the mouth
senses.definition: either of the two soft, movable edges that close the mouth
senses.definitionCN: 闭合嘴部的两片柔软、可活动的边缘
senses.example: He pressed his lips together and said nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 他抿紧嘴唇，什么也没说。
senses.why: Old English lippa named the fleshy edge of the mouth, and that body part is still the word's centre; every later sense is cut to its outline.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 lippa 指的就是嘴边的肉，这个身体部位至今仍是词的核心；后来每个义项都是照着它的轮廓剪出来的。

senses.title: The rim of a container or opening
senses.definition: the edge or rim of a container, hole or opening, especially one that curves outward
senses.definitionCN: 容器、洞口或开口的边缘，尤指略微向外翻的口沿
senses.example: She wiped the lip of the cup before pouring.
senses.exampleCN: 倒水之前她擦了擦杯口。
senses.why: A mouth is a soft edge around an opening, and a cup or a crater has the same outline; English borrows the body word for any raised rim.
senses.whyCN: 嘴是围在开口周围的一圈软边，杯子和火山口也有同样的轮廓；英语便借这个身体词来指任何凸起的边沿。

senses.title: Rude or disrespectful talk
senses.definition: rude or disrespectful remarks, especially when a younger person answers back
senses.definitionCN: 无礼、不敬的话，尤指晚辈对长辈顶嘴
senses.example: Don't give me any lip about the chores.
senses.exampleCN: 别为了家务跟我顶嘴。
senses.why: Speech comes out of the mouth, and the lip is the visible gate of the mouth; insolent words are pictured as something pushed through that gate.
senses.whyCN: 话从嘴里出来，嘴唇就是嘴看得见的门；无礼的话被想成硬从这扇门里推出来的东西。

senses.title: The lower petal of an orchid
senses.definition: the lower petal of an orchid, which is usually larger and differently shaped
senses.definitionCN: 兰花下方那片通常更大、形状也不同的花瓣
senses.example: The orchid's lip is marked with dark purple spots.
senses.exampleCN: 这朵兰花下方的唇瓣上带着深紫色的斑点。
senses.why: Botanists needed a name for the petal that hangs out like a lower lip, and the everyday body word was ready at hand.
senses.whyCN: 植物学家需要给那片像下唇一样探出来的花瓣起名，手边现成的身体词正好可用。

intro.en: Lip is an Old English word for the edge of the mouth; its Germanic relatives are close, but the path further back is uncertain.
intro.cn: lip 是古英语中表示「嘴的边缘」的词；它在日耳曼语族中的亲属很近，但再往前追溯则来源不确定。

items.en: Old English records lippa for the edge of the mouth, a weak noun that already meant the body part.
items.cn: 古英语用 lippa 指嘴的边缘，这是个弱变化名词，当时已经专指这个身体部位。

items.en: The word belongs to a Germanic family with Dutch lip and German Lippe; the reconstructed ancestor is usually written with a doubled consonant, though its exact shape is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词属于一个日耳曼语族，与荷兰语 lip、德语 Lippe 同族；重构的祖形通常写作带双辅音的形式，但确切形态不确定。

items.en: Beyond Germanic the origin is uncertain; a link with Latin labium has been suggested but is not reliably established.
items.cn: 再往上追溯来源不确定；有人提出它与拉丁语 labium 有关，但并未可靠证实。

items.en: Middle English lippe continues the bodily sense and settles the modern spelling without adding new meanings.
items.cn: 中古英语的 lippe 延续了身体部位的义项，并稳定了现代拼写，没有增加新的意思。

items.en: Modern English extends lip to the rim of vessels, to insolent speech, and to the lip-shaped petal of an orchid.
items.cn: 现代英语把 lip 扩展到器皿的口沿、无礼的言语，以及兰花的唇状花瓣。

note.en: The look-alike group collects compounds and derivatives built on lip plus one Latin word for a lip; the near-meaning group collects words for mouths and edges.
note.cn: 形近组收由 lip 构成的复合词、派生词，以及一个意为「唇」的拉丁词；近义组收表示嘴与边缘的词。

entries.definition: Coloured cosmetic for the lips.
entries.definitionCN: 口红；由 lip 与 stick 复合而成。

entries.definition: Inclined to answer back rudely.
entries.definitionCN: 爱顶嘴的；由 lip 加 -y 构成。

entries.definition: To understand speech by watching the speaker's lips.
entries.definitionCN: 看口型读懂话；由 lip 与 read 复合。

entries.definition: A Latin word for a lip, also used in anatomy for a lip-like fold.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中表示「唇」的词，解剖学也用来指唇状褶；它与 lip 只是意义相近，拼写与词源都不同。

entries.definition: The whole opening in the face used for eating and speaking.
entries.definitionCN: 嘴；脸上用来进食和说话的整个开口，lip 只是它的一部分。

entries.definition: The outer edge of a round or curved object.
entries.definitionCN: 圆形或弧形物体的外缘。

entries.definition: The outside limit of an object or area.
entries.definitionCN: 物体或区域的边缘。

entries.definition: The top edge of a cup or the projecting edge of a hat.
entries.definitionCN: 杯口的上沿；帽檐。

normalIntro.en: The word is a short Germanic noun for the edge of the mouth, and its family keeps returning to soft rims and openings.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个简短的日耳曼语名词，指嘴的边缘；它的同族词反复回到柔软的边沿与开口。

normal.en: Old English lippa already meant the edge of the mouth, so the body part is the oldest sense and the others borrow its outline.
normal.cn: 古英语 lippa 已经指嘴的边缘，所以身体部位是最早的义项，其他义项都借用了它的轮廓。

normal.en: Dutch lip and German Lippe are close cousins, and the short word has stayed almost unchanged around the North Sea.
normal.cn: 荷兰语 lip 和德语 Lippe 是近亲，这个短词在北海两岸几乎原样保留了下来。

normal.en: Lipstick puts lip in front of stick, and the compound never loses the mouth at its centre.
normal.cn: lipstick 把 lip 放在 stick 前面，这个复合词始终没有丢掉中心那个「嘴」。

normal.en: A cup has a lip because a cup and a mouth are both soft edges around an opening.
normal.cn: 杯子有 lip，是因为杯子和嘴都是围在开口周围的一圈软边。

normal.en: To give someone lip is to push rude words through the same gate that lets food in.
normal.cn: 对某人 give lip，就是把无礼的话从同一扇也放食物进来的门里推出去。

abstract.en: A lip is a border that can open, which makes it a fitting image for the edge of anything that must let something through.
abstract.cn: 嘴唇是一道能开的边界，很适合用来比喻任何必须放东西通过的边缘。

abstract.en: The same word covers a mouth, a cup and a crater because all three are openings with a raised rim.
abstract.cn: 同一个词覆盖嘴、杯子和火山口，因为这三者都是带凸起边沿的开口。

abstract.en: Silence is often described as pressed lips, a reminder that the mouth's edge can shut as well as speak.
abstract.cn: 沉默常被写成抿紧的双唇，这提醒人：嘴的边缘既能说话，也能关上。

examples.en: He pressed his lips together and said nothing.
examples.cn: 他抿紧嘴唇，什么也没说。

examples.en: She wiped the lip of the cup before pouring.
examples.cn: 倒水之前她擦了擦杯口。

examples.en: The orchid's lip is marked with dark purple spots.
examples.cn: 这朵兰花下方的唇瓣上带着深紫色的斑点。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「里普」——他顶着嘴说个不停，靠的就是这张嘴；lip 是嘴唇，也是杯口那道边。

root: 古英语 lippa（嘴唇）；与荷兰语 lip、德语 Lippe 同属一个日耳曼语族。更早的来源不确定，与拉丁语 labium（唇）的关系未获可靠证实。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the soft edge of the mouth; from it come the rim of any opening, the insolent words pushed through that gate, and the orchid petal shaped like a lip.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是嘴边的软边；由此分出任何开口的边沿、从这扇门推出去的无礼话，以及形状像唇的兰花花瓣。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two soft lips pressed together, closing an opening at its edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：两片柔软的嘴唇合在一起，在开口的边缘把它关上。

branches.en: two lips meeting in a quiet line
branches.cn: 两片嘴唇轻轻合拢成一条线

branches.en: a child answering back with a pout
branches.cn: 孩子嘟着嘴顶了一句

branches.en: a jug tipped at its rim
branches.cn: 壶口倾斜，水从边沿流出

branches.en: a flower whose lowest petal hangs like a lip
branches.cn: 一朵花最低的花瓣垂下来像一片唇

branches.en: words pushing out through the mouth
branches.cn: 话从嘴里推了出来

intro.en: The word is a short Germanic noun for the mouth's edge, and English builds compounds and a suffix on that base without adding a prefix.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个简短的日耳曼语名词，指嘴的边缘；英语在这个词基上造复合词、加后缀，却没有加前缀。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; Latin labium means lip, but the resemblance has not been shown to rest on a shared root.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；拉丁语 labium 意为「唇」，但相似之处尚未被证明来自共同词根。

items.meaning: to read speech from the lips

definition_zh: 液体的；液态的；流动而清澈的；（资产）易变现的；现金充裕的
definition_en: in the state of a substance that flows freely, clear and smooth, or easily converted into cash
core_image: 一只玻璃杯里水沿杯壁滑下，杯底的硬币清晰可见
scene: 孩子把杯子打翻，水沿着桌沿流下，滴在地板上。The child knocked the cup over and the liquid ran along the table edge onto the floor.
sceneCN: 这里指「能自由流动的液体」（第 1 个义项：有一定体积而无固定形状、可流动的物质状态）；句意为孩子打翻杯子，液体沿桌沿流下，滴到地板上。可辨识物件：玻璃杯、桌沿、水滴、地板；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 液体的；液态的；清澈流动的；（资产）易变现的

derivatives.zh: 基础形容词加名词后缀，表性质 → 流动性
基础词干加使动后缀 → 使液化
由该动词加名词后缀 → 液化
基础形容词加动词后缀，义为「使结清」→ 清算；变现
与基础词同出拉丁「流体」的旁系同源词 → 酒；液体

senses.title: A substance that flows freely
senses.titleCN: 能自由流动的物质状态
senses.definition: matter with a definite volume but no fixed shape, which takes the shape of its container
senses.definitionCN: 有一定体积而无固定形状、随容器改变形状的物质
senses.example: Mercury is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 汞是室温下唯一呈液态的金属。
senses.why: the adjective describes the state itself, and the noun names any substance in it, so the pair covers water, oil and melted metal.
senses.whyCN: 形容词描述这一状态本身，名词指处于该状态的任何物质，因此水、油与熔化的金属都包括在内。

senses.title: Clear and translucent, as light or eyes
senses.titleCN: 清澈透亮的，如光或眼睛
senses.definition: describing something that lets light through and looks deep rather than cloudy
senses.definitionCN: 描述透光、显得深澈而不浑浊之物
senses.example: The lake was liquid green in the early sun.
senses.exampleCN: 清晨阳光下，湖面泛着清澈的绿。
senses.why: clear water was the original sight behind the word, and the quality was transferred to anything that seems to hold light within.
senses.whyCN: 清水是这个词背后的原始景象，这一性质随后被移到任何仿佛内含光亮之物上。

senses.title: Smooth and flowing in movement or sound
senses.titleCN: 动作或声音的流畅圆润
senses.definition: describing motion or music that runs without jerks, like a stream
senses.definitionCN: 描述动作或音乐毫无顿挫、如水般流淌
senses.example: Her liquid phrasing made the sonata seem easy.
senses.exampleCN: 她流畅的乐句让这首奏鸣曲显得轻松。
senses.why: what flows without obstruction is pleasant to watch or hear, so the physical idea became a word of praise for grace.
senses.whyCN: 无阻流动之物看着听着都舒服，物理观念于是变成赞美优雅的词。

senses.title: Easily turned into cash
senses.definition: describing an asset that can be sold quickly without a loss
senses.definitionCN: 描述能迅速售出而不损失价值的资产
senses.example: Treasury bills are the most liquid asset in the market.
senses.exampleCN: 短期国库券是市场上最容易变现的资产。
senses.why: cash itself flows, so an asset that becomes cash at once is described with the same word as water.
senses.whyCN: 现金本身会流动，能立刻变成现金的资产便与水共用同一个词。

senses.title: A market with many ready buyers
senses.definition: describing a market where large orders are absorbed without moving the price much
senses.definitionCN: 描述能吸收大额订单而价格变动不大的市场
senses.example: The shares became liquid only after the index inclusion.
senses.exampleCN: 这些股票被纳入指数之后才变得易于成交。
senses.why: a market is liquid when orders wait on both sides, so a seller meets a buyer instead of waiting.
senses.whyCN: 市场两侧都挂着订单时才算易成交，卖方能直接遇到买方而不必等待。

senses.title: Cash and near-cash funds
senses.definition: describing money held in cash or in instruments that can be spent almost at once
senses.definitionCN: 描述以现金或几乎可即刻支用的票据持有的钱
senses.example: The firm kept half its wealth in liquid form.
senses.exampleCN: 这家企业把一半财富以现金形式持有。
senses.why: wealth kept as cash can be spent without selling anything, which is the financial form of the same flow.
senses.whyCN: 以现金持有的财富无需出售任何东西就能支用，这是同一流动在金融上的形态。

senses.title: A liquid consonant in phonetics
senses.definition: describing the sounds l and r, which flow into neighbouring sounds without friction
senses.definitionCN: 描述边音与颤音这类与相邻音平滑相接、不产生摩擦的音
senses.example: English has two liquid consonants in most analyses.
senses.exampleCN: 多数分析认为英语有两个流音。
senses.why: phonetics borrowed the flowing image because these sounds pass into their neighbours without a stop, unlike plosives.
senses.whyCN: 语音学借用「流动」意象，因为这些音与邻音相接而不阻塞，与爆破音不同。

senses.title: A liquid diet in medicine
senses.definition: describing food taken as fluids for a period, often after surgery or during illness
senses.definitionCN: 描述在术后或病中一段时间内以流体形式进食
senses.example: He was on a liquid diet for three days.
senses.exampleCN: 他吃了三天流食。
senses.why: the medical use narrows the adjective to what can be swallowed as fluid, which is the oldest physical sense applied to care.
senses.whyCN: 医学用法把这个形容词收窄到可以以流质吞下的食物，这是最古老的物理义被用在照护上。

senses.title: Fluid, unsettled conditions in society
senses.titleCN: 社会中流动不定的状态
senses.definition: describing social or economic arrangements that change constantly and have no fixed form
senses.definitionCN: 描述不断变化、没有固定形态的社会或经济安排
senses.example: Bauman described modern life as liquid because nothing keeps its shape for long.
senses.exampleCN: 鲍曼把现代生活称作液态的，因为没有东西能长久保持形状。
senses.why: the metaphor extends flow from matter to institutions: what is liquid cannot be grasped and held, only followed.
senses.whyCN: 这一隐喻把流动从物质扩展到制度：液态之物抓不住、握不牢，只能跟随。

intro.en: Liquid comes from Latin liquidus 'fluid, clear', from liquere 'to be fluid'. English took it in the fourteenth century as both adjective and noun. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: liquid 来自拉丁 liquidus「流动的、清澈的」，其动词为 liquere「呈液态」。英语于 14 世纪把它同时吸收为形容词与名词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Liquere meant 'to be fluid, to flow, to be clear'. Its earlier origin is uncertain, and the common reconstruction is a hypothesis rather than a proved form.
items.cn: liquere 意为「呈液态、流动、清澈」。其更早来源不确定，常见重构只是假说，并非已证形式。

items.en: Liquidus described water, oil and melted substances, and also clear light and a smooth style of speech.
items.cn: liquidus 描述水、油与熔化物，也用于清澈的光与平顺的言辞。

items.en: English liquid appears in the fourteenth century, at first for flowing matter; the noun and the adjective developed together.
items.cn: 英语 liquid 于 14 世纪出现，最初指流动的物质；名词与形容词同时发展。

items.en: Seventeenth-century grammars used liquid for sounds that flow into their neighbours, a technical borrowing of the water image.
items.cn: 17 世纪的语法学用 liquid 指流进邻音的音，这是对水的意象的技术性借用。

items.en: In the nineteenth century the adjective was applied to assets that turn into cash quickly, and liquid assets became a standard phrase.
items.cn: 到 19 世纪，这个形容词被用于能迅速变成现金的资产，「流动资产」成为标准说法。

items.en: The twentieth and twenty-first centuries extended it to social arrangements that will not hold their shape, as in liquid modernity.
items.cn: 20 与 21 世纪把它扩展到无法保持形状的社会安排，如「液态现代性」。

note.en: Group one holds words from the flowing root or close in shape; group two holds adjectives that describe fluids, clarity or easy sale.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「流动」词根或形近的词；第二组是描述流体、清澈或易售的其他形容词。

entries.definition: The ease of turning assets into cash; liquid is the adjective that carries the same idea.
entries.definitionCN: 指资产变现的容易程度；liquid 是承载同一观念的形容词。

entries.definition: A distilled alcoholic drink, from Latin liquor 'fluid'; the modern sense is a narrow survival.
entries.definitionCN: 指蒸馏酒，来自拉丁 liquor「流体」；现代义是狭窄的存留。

entries.definition: To sell off assets or wind up a firm; it names the action that makes a holding liquid.
entries.definitionCN: 指出售资产或结束企业；它指使持有物变现的动作。

entries.definition: To make something fluid; it is about physical state, not money.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某物液化；关乎物理状态，而非金钱。

entries.definition: A substance that flows; it is the everyday term, while liquid is the technical state between solid and gas.
entries.definitionCN: 指流动的物质；它是日常说法，liquid 是固气之间的技术状态。

entries.definition: Easy to see through; it covers the translucent sense but says nothing about flow or cash.
entries.definitionCN: 指容易看透；只覆盖清澈义，与流动或现金无关。

entries.definition: Free from bumps; it covers the flowing-motion sense but not the substance.
entries.definitionCN: 指没有凹凸；覆盖流畅义，但不指物质状态。

entries.definition: Able to find a buyer; liquid adds that the sale is fast and does not move the price.
entries.definitionCN: 指能寻得买家；liquid 另含「卖得快且不压价」。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Water is the original picture: it flows, it is clear, and it takes the shape of whatever holds it.
normal.cn: 水是原始图景：会流、清澈，并随容器改变形状。

normal.en: The family runs liquid, liquidity, liquefy, liquefaction, liquidate, liquor.
normal.cn: 同族词包括液体的、流动性、液化、液化过程、清算、蒸馏酒。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: liquid assets, liquid nitrogen, liquid crystal, liquid diet.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：流动资产、液氮、液晶、流食。

normal.en: In finance the test is simple: can it become cash this week without a discount?
normal.cn: 金融上的检验很简单：它这周能不能不折价地变成现金？

normal.en: In phonetics the same word names sounds that glide into their neighbours.
normal.cn: 在语音学中，同一个词指滑入邻音的那些音。

abstract.en: Picture water sliding down the inside of a glass while a coin at the bottom stays visible.
abstract.cn: 想象水沿杯壁滑下，杯底的硬币仍清晰可见。

abstract.en: Picture a stream that takes the shape of every stone it passes.
abstract.cn: 想象一条溪流，随经过的每块石头改变形状。

abstract.en: Picture a city where the buildings are replaced before anyone learns their names.
abstract.cn: 想象一座城市，楼房在人们记住名字之前就被替换。

examples.en: The doctor put him on a liquid diet for two days after the operation.
examples.cn: 手术后医生让他吃了两天流食。

examples.en: Investors moved into liquid assets as the outlook darkened.
examples.cn: 前景转暗时，投资者转向流动资产。

examples.en: The market is liquid enough for a large order to be filled in minutes.
examples.cn: 这个市场的流动性足以让大额订单在几分钟内成交。

dict_mnemonic.text: 这个词听起来像「流克的」——能流的、清亮的；钱能立刻流成现金，就是易变现的

root: 拉丁 liquidus「流动的、清澈的」来自 liquere「呈液态」，更深来源不确定；英语 14 世纪吸收为形容词与名词，17 世纪进入语音学，19 世纪进入金融。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow flow: a substance that flows, light that passes through it, motion that runs smoothly, an asset that becomes cash, a market that absorbs orders, funds kept in cash, a consonant that glides, a diet taken as fluid, and a society that will not hold its shape.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿「流动」展开：会流的物质、透过它的光、平滑的运行、变成现金的资产、能吸收订单的市场、以现金持有的资金、滑入邻音的音、以流质进食的饮食，以及无法保持形状的社会。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water sliding down a glass, clear enough to show the coin beneath.
core.cn: 核心意象：水沿玻璃杯滑下，清澈得能看见杯底的硬币。

branches.en: THE SUBSTANCE AND ITS CLARITY: what flows also lets light through, and both belong to water.
branches.cn: 物质与清澈：会流之物也让光透过，二者都属于水。

branches.en: SMOOTH PASSAGE: motion and consonants alike glide into what follows without a stop.
branches.cn: 平滑过渡：动作与辅音都不阻塞地滑入后接之物。

branches.en: MONEY THAT FLOWS: an asset becomes cash, and the firm keeps its wealth in that form.
branches.cn: 会流的钱：资产变成现金，企业以该形式持有财富。

branches.en: THE MARKET'S DEPTH: many ready buyers let a large order pass without moving the price.
branches.cn: 市场的深度：众多现成买家让大额订单通过而不推动价格。

branches.en: CARE AND METAPHOR: a diet taken as fluid, and a society whose arrangements will not hold their shape.
branches.cn: 照护与隐喻：以流质进食的饮食，以及安排无法定形的社会。

intro.en: Liquid is a Latin adjective for flowing or clear; the same root supplies the noun for liquidity, the verb for melting and the drink called liquor.
intro.cn: liquid 是表示「流动、清澈」的拉丁形容词；同一词根给出表示流动性的名词、表示熔化的动词，以及名为 liquor 的酒。

latinIntro.en: Latin liquere and liquidus stand behind this whole family, from liquid and liquidity to liquefy and liquor.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 liquere 与 liquidus 支撑整个词族，从 liquid、liquidity 到 liquefy 与 liquor。

items.example: The root is about water and light.
Liquid metal poured from the mould.
items.exampleCN: 液态金属从模具中倒出。

items.example: Keep the liquid away from the samples.

items.exampleCN: 流动性在数小时内消失。

items.example: The court ordered the firm liquidated.

items.meaning: one who winds up an estate

definition_zh: 清单；名单；名册；列出；把……列入名单；（船）倾斜
definition_en: a series of items or names written down in order, an official register, the act of setting such items down, or, of a ship, a lean to one side
core_image: 一条窄纸条上，名字从上往下一行行排好
scene: 出门买菜前，她把要买的东西一项项写在纸条上，写完折好塞进外套口袋。Before leaving for the market, she read the shopping list one more time.
sceneCN: 这里 list 是「清单」（第 1 个义项：把事项逐条写下来的单子）；句意为出门去市场之前，她又看了一遍购物清单。画面里可抓住的物件：窄纸条、折痕、外套口袋。

pos.zh: 列出；把……列入名单；（船）向一侧倾斜

derivatives.zh: 由 list 加 -ing 构成，指清单上的一条记录，也指挂牌信息或上市
由 list 的过去分词转作形容词，指已列入名单的、挂牌上市的
由 short 与 list 复合，指筛出的候选名单，或把人列入候选名单

senses.title: A series of items written down in order
senses.definition: a set of items, especially things to buy or do, written or printed one below another
senses.definitionCN: 把要买或要做的事项一条条写下来或印出来的单子
senses.example: She added eggs and bread to the shopping list.
senses.exampleCN: 她把鸡蛋和面包加进了购物清单。
senses.why: The oldest English list was not a page but a narrow strip of cloth or paper, an edge; once you write down such a strip, its shape alone turns the writing into a column of items, so the word moves from the material to what is written on it.
senses.whyCN: 古英语里 list 原指窄布条、纸条或边缘，而不是一整页；沿着这样的窄条往下写，光靠形状就把文字排成一列条目，于是词义从「材料」转到「写在上面的内容」。

senses.title: An official roll of names
senses.titleCN: 名册：为某一用途排好的名字
senses.definition: a register of names kept for a purpose, such as members, patients, or candidates
senses.definitionCN: 为某一用途保存的人名登记，如成员、病人或候选人名单
senses.example: The nurse checked the list of patients before the morning round.
senses.exampleCN: 护士在上午查房前核对了一遍病人名单。
senses.why: A strip of writing can be checked line by line, so institutions adopted the word for names kept in order; the list became a tool of record-keeping, which is why it appears with waiting, crew, and class.
senses.whyCN: 竖着写的窄条最适合一行行核对，机构便用这个词指按顺序保存的人名；list 由此成了登记工具，所以常与等候、船员、班级等词搭配。

senses.title: To set items or names down in order
senses.definition: to write or print items one after another, or to enter someone or something on an official record
senses.definitionCN: 把项目依次写出或印出，也指把某人某物登记进正式记录
senses.example: Please list the three books you found most useful.
senses.exampleCN: 请列出你觉得最有用的三本书。
senses.why: Because the noun already covered both the strip and the items on it, the verb needed no new shape: to list is simply to produce that column, whether on paper or in a database, and later to have one's name entered in a public record such as a stock exchange.
senses.whyCN: 名词已经同时指窄条和条上的条目，动词便不必另造形状：list 就是把这个竖列生产出来，无论写在纸上还是录进数据库；再往后，把名字登记进交易所这类公开记录也叫 list。

senses.title: Of a ship, to lean to one side
senses.definition: of a ship or boat, to lean or tilt to one side, especially because of wind, cargo, or damage
senses.definitionCN: 船或小艇因风、载重或破损而向一侧歪斜
senses.example: The old boat listed badly to port after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨过后，那条旧船严重向左舷倾斜。
senses.why: This nautical sense appears in the seventeenth century and its origin is uncertain; it may come from a Scandinavian word or from the older edge sense, and dictionaries treat it as a separate development that happens to share the spelling of the catalogue word.
senses.whyCN: 这个航海义项出现于十七世纪，来源不确定；它可能来自斯堪的纳维亚语，也可能与较早的「边缘」义有关，词典把它当作与「清单」同形而各自发展的一支。

intro.en: List began as a word for a narrow strip or edge; the catalogue sense may have come through French, and the nautical sense of leaning is of uncertain origin.
intro.cn: list 最初指窄条或边缘；「清单、名册」义可能经法语而来；表示船身倾斜的义项来源不确定。

items.en: *līstōn meant a strip, edge, or border; the asterisk marks a reconstructed form rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: *līstōn 意为窄条、边缘或边界；星号表示这是重构形式，并非有记录的原词。

items.en: Old English līste named the edge of cloth and later a strip of paper, the shape on which a column of writing fits.
items.cn: 古英语 līste 指布料边缘，后来也指纸条，正是竖排文字所依附的形状。

items.en: Old French liste, a roll or catalogue, may have strengthened the sense of a list of names; its own origin is uncertain and may be Germanic.
items.cn: 古法语的 liste 指名册或目录，可能强化了「名单」义；它本身的来源不确定，可能来自日耳曼语。

items.en: Middle English used liste for both the strip and the written roll, so the material and its contents merged.
items.cn: 中古英语的 liste 兼指窄条与写好的卷册，材料与内容由此合并。

items.en: Modern English keeps the noun for items and names, adds the verb to list, and keeps a separate nautical verb meaning to lean.
items.cn: 现代英语保留指条目与名字的名词，增加动词「列出」，并另有一个表示「倾斜」的航海动词。

note.en: The look-alike group collects compounds and words spelled with list; the near-meaning group collects other words for ordered records.
note.cn: 形近组收含 list 的复合词与拼写相近的词；近义组收其他表示有序记录的词。

entries.definition: Without energy or enthusiasm; it comes from an old sense of list meaning desire, not from a catalogue.
entries.definitionCN: 无精打采的；它来自 list 表示「愿望」的古义，与清单无关，只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: To join the army, or to obtain help or support.
entries.definitionCN: 入伍；争取帮助或支持。

entries.definition: A list of things to be checked or done.
entries.definitionCN: 核对或待办事项的清单。

entries.definition: A small list of chosen candidates.
entries.definitionCN: 筛出的少量候选人名单。

entries.definition: A complete list of items, often arranged in a system.
entries.definitionCN: 完整而系统排列的目录。

entries.definition: A list of goods or property, often with counts.
entries.definitionCN: 货物或财产的清单，常带数量。

entries.definition: An official book or record of names and details.
entries.definitionCN: 正式登记姓名与信息的簿册。

entries.definition: A list of people and their duties or turns.
entries.definitionCN: 人员及其职责或轮值的名单。

normalIntro.en: The word is held together by an Old English noun for a strip and a French roll of names, with two English compounds built on it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由表示窄条的古英语名词与表示名册的法语词共同撑起，另有两个建立在它之上的英语复合词。

normal.en: The oldest list was a strip of cloth or paper, so picture a narrow column rather than a whole page.
normal.cn: 最早的 list 是一条窄布或窄纸，所以要想象一条竖直的窄栏，而不是一整页。

normal.en: List as a verb needs no new ending: the noun already held both the strip and the items.
normal.cn: list 作动词不必另加词尾：名词本身已经同时包含窄条与条目。

normal.en: Checklist and shortlist are list with a qualifier in front, one for checking and one for a chosen few.
normal.cn: checklist 与 shortlist 都是在 list 前面加限定成分，一个用于核对，一个用于精选。

normal.en: A waiting list is a queue written down, so the word keeps the idea of names arranged in order.
normal.cn: waiting list 就是写下来的队列，这个词始终保留「名字按顺序排列」的意思。

normal.en: The leaning ship uses the same spelling but a different history, so context decides which list you are reading.
normal.cn: 倾斜的船用的是同一拼写却有另一段历史，所以要看上下文判断读的是哪个 list。

abstract.en: A strip becomes a column, and a column becomes an institution's memory.
abstract.cn: 窄条变成竖栏，竖栏又变成机构的记忆。

abstract.en: To list is to decide what deserves a line and, by implication, what does not.
abstract.cn: 列出就是决定什么值得占一行，也等于决定什么不值得。

abstract.en: Two words can wear one spelling and still come from different places, as the ship and the catalogue show.
abstract.cn: 两个词可以共用一种拼写却来自不同地方，船与清单就是例子。

examples.en: She added eggs and bread to the shopping list.
examples.cn: 她把鸡蛋和面包加进了购物清单。

examples.en: The nurse checked the list of patients before the round.
examples.cn: 护士在查房前核对了病人名单。

examples.en: The boat listed to one side as the wind grew stronger.
examples.cn: 风越来越大，小船向一侧倾斜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「立事特」——要办的事立起来排成一条，就是清单；list 是清单、列出。

root: 古英语 līste（窄条、边缘）是这个词的起点；「清单、名册」义可能经古法语 liste 加强，来源不确定；「船身倾斜」为另一支，来源不确定。没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a narrow written column; from it come the item list, the official roll of names, the verb that produces them, and a separate nautical sense of leaning.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一条写满字的窄栏；由此分出事项清单、正式名册、产生清单的动词，以及另成一系的「船身倾斜」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow strip of paper with names written down it, one under another.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条窄纸条，名字从上往下一行行写下去。

branches.en: a shopping list folded into a coat pocket
branches.cn: 折好塞进外套口袋的购物清单

branches.en: names running down a narrow strip of paper
branches.cn: 名字沿窄纸条往下排

branches.en: a clipboard with patients listed by room
branches.cn: 按病房列好病人的病历板

branches.en: a hand adding a new line to a column
branches.cn: 一只手在竖栏里添上新的一行

branches.en: a fishing boat leaning hard to port
branches.cn: 渔船的船身严重向左舷倾斜

intro.en: The word is supported by an Old English noun for a strip, a French roll of names, and two English compounds built on list.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示窄条的古英语名词、表示名册的法语词，以及两个建立在 list 之上的英语复合词共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin lista is a borrowing from Germanic or Old French, so no native Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 lista 借自日耳曼语或古法语，因此这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaningCN: 按顺序写下的条目或名字

definition_zh: 听；倾听；听从；留心等着听；偷听
definition_en: to give deliberate attention to sound, to heed what is said, to wait for a particular sound, or to overhear a conversation
core_image: 一个人停下手里的活，侧耳朝向声音来源
scene: 夜里屋子很静，母亲关掉电视，侧耳对着楼上婴儿床的方向。She turned down the radio and listened for the baby's cry.
sceneCN: 这里 listen 是「留心等着听」（第 3 个义项：等某个声音出现）；句意为她调低收音机，等着听婴儿的哭声。画面里可抓住的物件：关掉的电视、楼上的婴儿床、调低的音量。

pos.zh: 听；倾听；听从；留心等着听；偷听

derivatives.zh: 由 listen 加 -er 构成，指听的人，尤指收听节目的听众
由 listen 加 -ing 构成，指听的行为，也指用心倾听的
由 listen 加 -able 构成，指听着不难受、值得一听的

senses.title: To give attention to sound
senses.titleCN: 听：把注意力放到声音上
senses.definition: to give deliberate attention to a sound or to someone speaking
senses.definitionCN: 有意识地把注意力放在某个声音或某人的说话上
senses.example: She listened to the rain on the roof until she fell asleep.
senses.exampleCN: 她听着屋顶上的雨声，直到睡着。
senses.why: Old English had hlysnan for attending to sound beside hyran for simply hearing; the two verbs split the work, and listen took the side of effort and attention rather than passive reception.
senses.whyCN: 古英语里 hlysnan 表示注意地听，hyran 表示听见；两个动词分工，listen 占了「费心去听」这一边，而不是被动接收。

senses.title: To heed advice or a warning
senses.titleCN: 听从：把听到的话当回事
senses.definition: to pay attention to advice, a warning, or a request and act on it
senses.definitionCN: 重视劝告、警告或请求并照着去做
senses.example: He never listens to his doctor about sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 他从不听医生关于睡眠的建议。
senses.why: Hearing turns into obedience when the listener acts on what was said; the same verb slides from the ear to behaviour, which is why listen to reason and listen to your parents sound natural.
senses.whyCN: 当听的人照着话去做，听见就变成了服从；同一个动词从耳朵滑到行为，所以 listen to reason（听劝）和听父母的话都很自然。

senses.title: To wait and watch for a particular sound
senses.titleCN: 留心等着听：等某个声音出现
senses.definition: to keep one's attention on the possibility of a particular sound, especially in order to respond
senses.definitionCN: 把注意力放在某个可能出现的声响上，以便及时反应
senses.example: The guard listened for footsteps on the stairs.
senses.exampleCN: 守卫留神听着楼梯上的脚步声。
senses.why: The preposition for turns listening into a search: nothing has been heard yet, and the ear is held open for a signal, as in listen for the doorbell.
senses.whyCN: 介词 for 把「听」变成「找」：此刻还没有声音，只是把耳朵开着等一个信号，如留神听门铃。

senses.title: To overhear others on purpose
senses.titleCN: 偷听：躲在暗处听别人说话
senses.definition: to hear a conversation that is not meant for you, often by staying hidden or by using a device
senses.definitionCN: 听到并非说给自己听的谈话，常靠躲藏或借助设备
senses.example: Someone was listening in on the meeting from the next room.
senses.exampleCN: 有人躲在隔壁房间偷听会议。
senses.why: The particle in adds the idea of entering a space that is not yours, so listen in on marks the listener as an outsider who was never invited.
senses.whyCN: 小品词 in 加进「进入不属于自己的空间」的意思，所以 listen in on 把听者标成未被邀请的外人。

intro.en: Listen goes back to a Germanic verb for hearing with attention; the h of its Old English form was later dropped, and the word is widely linked to the root behind loud.
intro.cn: listen 源自日耳曼语中表示「用心听」的动词；古英语形式里的 h 后来被丢掉，一般认为它与 loud 同源。

items.en: The reconstructed root *ḱlew- meant to hear, and it also underlies words for fame, since being heard of is being talked about.
items.cn: 重构词根 *ḱlew- 意为「听见」，也衍生出表示名声的词，因为被人听说就是被人谈论。

items.en: *hlusinōn, a verb of listening, grew beside *hlūdaz, the adjective that became loud; both point back to the act of hearing.
items.cn: *hlusinōn 是表示「听」的动词，与后来变成 loud 的形容词 *hlūdaz 并生；两者都指向「听见」这一行为。

items.en: Old English wrote the verb as hlysnan, with an h that speakers later stopped pronouncing.
items.cn: 古英语把动词写作 hlysnan，词首的 h 后来在口语中不再发音。

items.en: Middle English settled on listen, dropped the h in spelling, and kept the meaning of giving ear to something.
items.cn: 中古英语定型为 listen，拼写中去掉 h，保留「把耳朵给某物」的意思。

items.en: Modern English adds listener and listening, and the phrasal forms listen in and listen up, which push the word toward eavesdropping and toward a call for attention.
items.cn: 现代英语派生 listener 与 listening，并发展出 listen in、listen up 等短语，把词义推向偷听与提醒注意。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built with listen; the near-meaning group separates deliberate listening from mere hearing and from related acts of attention.
note.cn: 形近组收由 listen 构成的词形；近义组把刻意的「听」与单纯的「听见」以及相关的注意行为区分开。

entries.definition: A person who listens, especially to a radio programme.
entries.definitionCN: 听的人；收听节目的听众。

entries.definition: The act of paying attention to sound, or an adjective for such activity.
entries.definitionCN: 听的行为；用心倾听的。

entries.definition: Pleasant or easy enough to listen to.
entries.definitionCN: 听着不难受、值得一听的。

entries.definition: A written series of items or names; the two words are only close in spelling and sound, with different origins.
entries.definitionCN: 写下来的条目或名单；与 listen 只是拼写发音相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To receive sound, often without deliberate attention.
entries.definitionCN: 听见，常指并非刻意去听。

entries.definition: To pay careful attention to advice or a warning.
entries.definitionCN: 留意并重视劝告或警告。

entries.definition: To hear something by chance, without intending to.
entries.definitionCN: 无意中听到。

entries.definition: To listen secretly to a private conversation.
entries.definitionCN: 偷听私人谈话。

normalIntro.en: The word is carried by an Old English verb, its lost h, a Germanic root shared with loud, and English endings that make a listener and a listening.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由古英语动词、失落了的 h、与 loud 共有的日耳曼词根，以及构成 listener 与 listening 的英语词尾共同支撑。

normal.en: Old English wrote the verb with an h, so the silent letter in today's spelling is a leftover, not a rule about pronunciation.
normal.cn: 古英语写法带 h，所以今天拼写里的不发音字母是遗留物，并不是发音规则。

normal.en: Listener is listen plus -er, the person at the receiving end of the sound.
normal.cn: listener 是 listen 加 -er，指声音接收端的那个人。

normal.en: Hear is what happens to you; listen is what you decide to do, and English keeps both verbs.
normal.cn: hear 是发生在你身上的事，listen 是你决定去做的事，英语把两个动词都保留下来。

normal.en: Listen for waits for a signal; listen to receives what is already there; the preposition marks the difference.
normal.cn: listen for 是等一个信号，listen to 是接收已经在那里的声音，介词标出了这个差别。

normal.en: Listen in on adds in because the listener steps into a space where he was not invited.
normal.cn: listen in on 之所以加 in，是因为听者走进了没有邀请他的空间。

abstract.en: To listen is to lend someone your ears for a while, which is why the verb so easily turns into obedience.
abstract.cn: 倾听是把耳朵借给别人一段时间，所以这个动词很容易变成服从。

abstract.en: Attention has a direction: you can listen to, listen for, or listen in, and each preposition draws a different boundary.
abstract.cn: 注意力是有方向的：可以 listen to、listen for、listen in，每个介词都画出不同的边界。

abstract.en: A word for hearing can grow into a word for trust, because people who are heard are also more likely to be followed.
abstract.cn: 表示「听」的词能长成表示「信任」的词，因为被听见的人也更容易被跟随。

examples.en: She listened to the rain until she fell asleep.
examples.cn: 她听着雨声直到睡着。

examples.en: The guard listened for footsteps on the stairs.
examples.cn: 守卫留神听着楼梯上的脚步声。

examples.en: He never listens to his doctor.
examples.cn: 他从不听医生的劝。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「力森」——用力把声音收进耳朵，就是倾听；listen 是听。

root: 古英语 hlysnan（用心听）来自日耳曼语 *hlusinōn，词首 h 后来失落；一般认为与 loud 同源，并可上溯到重构词根 *ḱlew-（听见）；拉丁语 cluere（闻名）也出自这一词根，只是词义已转向「被谈论」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is deliberate attention to sound; it divides into obedience to what is said, waiting for a signal, and listening where one is not welcome.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是刻意把注意力放在声音上；由此分出听从所说的话、等候某个信号，以及在不被欢迎的地方偷听。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person stopping work and turning one ear toward the source of a sound.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人停下手里的活，侧耳朝向声音的来源。

branches.en: a head tilted toward rain on a roof
branches.cn: 头侧向屋顶的雨声

branches.en: an ear kept open while nothing is heard yet
branches.cn: 什么都还没听见，耳朵却已经开着

branches.en: a patient nodding at the doctor's advice
branches.cn: 病人对医生的嘱咐点头

branches.en: a guard holding still for footsteps
branches.cn: 守卫静止不动等脚步声

branches.en: a door left ajar beside a meeting
branches.cn: 会议旁虚掩着的一扇门

intro.en: The word is carried by an Old English verb, its lost h, a Germanic root shared with loud, and English suffixes that make a listener and a listening.
intro.cn: 这个词由古英语动词、失落的 h、与 loud 共有的日耳曼词根，以及构成 listener 与 listening 的英语后缀支撑。

latinIntro.en: The same reconstructed root is thought to lie behind Latin cluere 'to be spoken of' and its adjective inclutus 'famous', where hearing has shifted into reputation.
latinIntro.cn: 一般认为同一重构词根也留在拉丁语 cluere（被谈论）及其形容词 inclutus（有名的）里，那里「听见」已经转向「名声」。

items.meaning: the act of attending to sound

latinEntries.meaning: to be spoken of, to be renowned

definition_zh: 按字面；逐字地；确实地；简直（口语夸张用法）
definition_en: in a literal sense or word for word, in fact, or, informally, as a strong intensifier with little literal truth
core_image: 手指沿着印刷的一行字，一个字母一个字母移过去
scene: 朋友把一句玩笑当成真话，还认真追问细节，旁边的人忍不住笑。She took his joke literally and began checking the figures.
sceneCN: 这里 literally 是「按字面」（第 1 个义项：照词语本义理解）；句意是她把玩笑按字面当真，开始核对数字。画面里可抓住的动作：朋友认真追问、旁人的笑、纸上待核对的数字。

pos.zh: 按字面；逐字地；确实地；简直

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 littera（字母）加 -al 构成，指字面的、照字面理解的
由 literal 加 -ness 构成，指拘泥字面的性质
由 literal 加 -ism 构成，指拘泥字面、字面主义的做法
由 literal 加 -ist 构成，指死抠字面的人

senses.title: In the literal sense of the words
senses.titleCN: 按字面：照词语本来的意思
senses.definition: in the ordinary, literal meaning of the words used, rather than in a figurative or exaggerated one
senses.definitionCN: 按所用词语的本义去理解，而不是按比喻或夸张的意思
senses.example: The phrase was meant literally, not as a joke.
senses.exampleCN: 这句话是按字面意思说的，不是开玩笑。
senses.why: The word is built on Latin littera, a letter of the alphabet, so literally begins as 'according to the letters': you read what the words actually say, and no picture is allowed to stand in for them.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在拉丁语 littera（字母）之上，literally 的起点是「按照字母」：你读的是词语实际写出的内容，不许任何比喻顶替它。

senses.title: Word for word
senses.definition: word for word, following the exact order and wording of the original
senses.definitionCN: 逐字照原话的顺序与措辞，不作改动
senses.example: The contract was translated literally, so the jokes disappeared.
senses.exampleCN: 合同是逐字翻译的，所以笑话全没了。
senses.why: If you follow the letters one by one, you also follow the words in their original order; translation done this way keeps the surface and loses the idiom.
senses.whyCN: 如果一个字母一个字母地跟着走，也就按原来的顺序跟着词走；这样翻译保住了表面，却丢掉了习语。

senses.title: In fact, really
senses.titleCN: 确实地：强调事情真的发生
senses.definition: actually, really, without exaggeration, used to stress that something surprising is true
senses.definitionCN: 确实、真的，不带夸张，用来强调某件令人意外的事是真的
senses.example: The team literally ran out of paper on the last day.
senses.exampleCN: 团队在最后一天确实把纸用完了。
senses.why: Because 'according to the letters' means 'according to the facts as stated', the adverb can certify a statement: what sounds like an exaggeration is being claimed as plain truth.
senses.whyCN: 既然「按字面」就是「按写明的事实」，这个副词就能为陈述作证：听起来像夸张的话，其实是在说大实话。

senses.title: As an intensifier, almost
senses.titleCN: 口语夸张用法：简直、几乎（并不字面）
senses.definition: used in informal speech as a strong intensifier, often when the statement is not literally true
senses.definitionCN: 口语中作强烈的加强词，常用于所述并非字面真实的情况
senses.example: I literally died laughing at that video.
senses.exampleCN: 那个视频简直把我笑死了。
senses.why: Intensifiers wear out and are borrowed from stronger words; speakers reached for literally to mark emphasis, and the very word for exactness became a badge of exaggeration, a usage dictionaries now record.
senses.whyCN: 加强词会磨损，于是从更有力的词里借用；说话人抓来 literally 表示强调，结果这个专管精确的词反倒成了夸张的标记，词典如今已收录这种用法。

intro.en: Literally is an English adverb built on literal, which descends from Latin littera, a letter of the alphabet.
intro.cn: literally 是英语副词，建立在 literal 之上，而 literal 源自拉丁语 littera（字母）。

items.en: Littera meant a letter of the alphabet, and in the plural litterae it could mean a letter, a document, or learning.
items.cn: littera 指字母，复数 litterae 可指书信、文书或学问。

items.en: Late Latin litteralis meant 'of letters' and described meaning that stays with the written words.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 litteralis 意为「字母的」，用来描述紧贴字面文字的涵义。

items.en: English took literal in the fifteenth century for meaning that follows the letter rather than the spirit.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪引入 literal，指跟随字面而非精神的理解。

items.en: Literally was formed with -ly soon after, first for word-for-word rendering and then for stating plain fact.
items.cn: literally 随后由 -ly 构成，先表逐字表达，再表陈述直白的事实。

items.en: In the twentieth century the intensifier use spread in speech, and it is now recorded, though still criticised in formal writing.
items.cn: 二十世纪里，加强语气的用法在口语中扩散，如今已被收录，但在正式写作中仍有争议。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the Latin stem for letter; the near-meaning group collects adverbs of exactness and reality.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「字母」词干上的词；近义组收表示精确与真实的副词。

entries.definition: Following the basic meaning of the words.
entries.definitionCN: 按词语本义的；字面的。

entries.definition: The ability to read and write, built on the same stem for letters.
entries.definitionCN: 读写能力，同样建立在「字母」词干上。

entries.definition: Written works, from the same stem as letters.
entries.definitionCN: 文学作品，与「字母」同一词干。

entries.definition: A written symbol or message, from the same Latin word.
entries.definitionCN: 字母或书信，来自同一个拉丁词。

entries.definition: Relating to literature or written language.
entries.definitionCN: 与文学或书面语言有关的。

entries.definition: In a precise way, with nothing added or left out.
entries.definitionCN: 精确地，不增不减。

entries.definition: In fact, as opposed to what was expected.
entries.definitionCN: 事实上，与预期相对。

entries.definition: In a genuine or sincere way.
entries.definitionCN: 真正地；真诚地。

entries.definition: In effect or almost, though not strictly.
entries.definitionCN: 实际上；几乎，虽非严格如此。

normalIntro.en: Literal comes from a Latin noun for a letter, so the adverb is a word about reading the letters in front of you.
normalIntro.cn: literal 来自拉丁语中表示字母的名词，所以这个副词是一个关于「读眼前字母」的词。

normal.en: Literal comes from littera, a letter, so a literal reading stays with the letters in front of you.
normal.cn: literal 来自 littera（字母），所以字面阅读就是紧跟着眼前的字母。

normal.en: Add -ly and the adjective becomes the adverb that says how the reading is done.
normal.cn: 加上 -ly，形容词就变成说明「怎样读」的副词。

normal.en: Translate literally is word for word; translate freely is by sense, and the two labels mark opposite choices.
normal.cn: 逐字翻译是跟着词走，意译是跟着意思走，两个说法标出相反的选择。

normal.en: Literally true certifies a surprising fact, so the word is doing the work of really.
normal.cn: literally true 是在为一件意外的事实作证，这个词在做 really 的活。

normal.en: A sentence like I literally died is not literal at all, which shows the intensifier has drifted from its root.
normal.cn: 像「我简直死了」这样的句子一点也不是字面意思，可见这个加强词已经漂离了词根。

abstract.en: A word built on letters becomes a word for truth, and then for emphasis, and the direction of travel is worth noticing.
abstract.cn: 一个建立在字母上的词变成了表示真实的词，又变成加强词，这个移动方向值得注意。

abstract.en: Exactness is a surface; when a sentence is read only at the surface, the joke or the metaphor is lost.
abstract.cn: 精确只是表面；只按表面读一句话，玩笑或隐喻就丢了。

abstract.en: The strongest claim of literalness can end up producing the least literal sentence.
abstract.cn: 最卖力声称字面的一句话，可能恰恰最不字面。

examples.en: The phrase was meant literally, not as a joke.
examples.cn: 这句话是按字面意思说的，不是玩笑。

examples.en: The contract was translated literally.
examples.cn: 这份合同是逐字翻译的。

examples.en: The team literally ran out of paper.
examples.cn: 团队确实把纸用完了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「李特柔利」——把每个字都照原样读出来，literally 是字面地。

root: 拉丁语 littera（字母）→ 晚期拉丁语 litteralis（字母的；字面的）→ 英语 literal → 加 -ly 成 literally；核心义「按字面」，后发展出「确实」与口语夸张用法。

sensesIntro.en: The core is reading by the letters; it branches into word-for-word rendering, into certifying plain fact, and into the looser intensifier use of speech.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是照着字母读；由此分出逐字翻译、为事实作证，以及口语里较松的夸张加强用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger moving letter by letter across a line of print.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指沿着印刷的一行字，一个字母一个字母地移过去。

branches.en: a reader stopping at the exact words on the page
branches.cn: 读者停在页面上确切的词句

branches.en: a translator following the original word by word
branches.cn: 译者逐词跟着原文

branches.en: a report confirming that the shortage was real
branches.cn: 报告确认短缺确有其事

branches.en: a friend insisting that the exaggeration really happened
branches.cn: 朋友坚称那句夸张的话真发生过

branches.en: the gap between the word and what it now claims
branches.cn: 词与它如今声称的东西之间的缝

intro.en: The word is built from a Latin noun for a letter, a Late Latin adjective, and two English suffixes that make an adjective and an adverb.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示字母的拉丁语名词、晚期拉丁语形容词，以及构成形容词与副词的两个英语后缀组成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun littera and its derivative adjective litteralis supply the whole family, and English keeps the stem in literal, literary and literature.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语名词 littera 及其派生形容词 litteralis 提供了整族词，英语在 literal、literary 与 literature 里保留了这一词干。

definition_en: relating to literature or to writing valued as art, and also describing a formal bookish style rather than everyday speech

scene: 深夜的书房里，台灯照着摊开的旧小说，读的人反复摩挲着发软的纸页。Her literary taste was shaped by the novels she read late at night.

由同一词干加 -cy 构成，义为「读写能力」

senses.title: Relating to literature
senses.definition: connected with literature, especially novels, poems and plays that are valued as art
senses.definitionCN: 与文学有关的，尤指与被视为艺术的小说、诗歌和戏剧有关
senses.example: She has a keen literary taste and reads a novel every week.
senses.exampleCN: 她文学品味敏锐，每周读一本小说。
senses.why: Latin littera meant a letter of the alphabet, and writing made of letters grew into literature; literary simply points back to that body of writing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 littera 意为字母，由字母写成的文字逐渐长成文学；literary 就是回头指向这一整片写作。

senses.title: Typical of formal written language
senses.definition: of a word or style, formal and at home in books rather than in ordinary conversation
senses.definitionCN: 指词语或文风正式，常见于书本，而不用于日常对话
senses.example: The word behold is literary rather than conversational.
senses.exampleCN: behold 这个词是书面语，而不是日常口语。
senses.why: A word that has left the street but survives in books is labelled by the place where it still lives; literary records the shelf, not the age of the word.
senses.whyCN: 一个词从街头消失却仍在书中存活，就被按它如今的栖身之处来标注；literary 记下的是书架，不是这个词的年岁。

senses.title: Having the quality of artful writing
senses.definition: showing the imagination and craft associated with good literature
senses.definitionCN: 显出与优秀文学作品相联系的想象力与写作技艺
senses.example: His account of the journey has a literary quality that makes it memorable.
senses.exampleCN: 他对这次旅程的记述有一种文学性的质地，让人读过难忘。
senses.why: Literature is writing judged for craft as well as content; when a passage invites that judgment, the adjective follows it from the shelf into the sentence.
senses.whyCN: 文学是既看内容也看手笔的文字；当一段话引来这种品评时，这个形容词便跟着它从书架走进句子，形容那段文字本身的质地。

senses.title: Connected with the profession of letters
senses.titleCN: 从事文学的；文学工作的
senses.definition: involving writers, books and the business or study that surrounds them, as in a literary agent or a literary magazine
senses.definitionCN: 涉及作家、书籍以及围绕它们的行业或研究，如文学经纪人、文学杂志
senses.example: The literary agent read the manuscript and offered a contract.
senses.exampleCN: 那位文学经纪人读完稿子，给了出版合同。
senses.why: Books support a small industry of editors, agents and magazines; literary names that professional world because it exists to produce and sell literature.
senses.whyCN: 书籍养活了编辑、经纪人和杂志组成的小行业；literary 指的就是这个职业圈子，因为它的存在就是为了生产和销售文学。

intro.en: Literary descends from the Latin word for a letter, and it still points to writing that is made of letters and valued as art.
intro.cn: literary 源自拉丁语中表示「字母」的词，至今仍指向由字母写成、并被当作艺术来欣赏的文字。

items.en: Littera named a letter of the alphabet, and in the plural it could name a written document or an epistle.
items.cn: littera 指字母表中的一个字母，复数形式还可指文书或书信。

items.en: The adjective litterarius meant of letters or of writing, and it covered both the skill of reading and the study of texts.
items.cn: 形容词 litterarius 意为与字母、书写有关的，既指读写技能，也指对文本的研究。

items.en: Old French reshaped the Latin adjective as literaire, keeping the sense of letters, learning and written culture.
items.cn: 古法语把拉丁形容词改写为 literaire，保留了文字、学问与书面文化的意味。

items.en: English borrowed the French form as literary in the seventeenth century, when literature was coming to mean fine writing rather than learning in general.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语借入法语形式，写作 literary；当时 literature 正从泛指学问转向指精美的写作。

items.en: Modern English keeps literary for the art of writing, for its formal register, and for the people and institutions that surround books.
items.cn: 现代英语用 literary 指写作的艺术、其正式语体，以及围绕书籍的人和机构。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin word for a letter; the near-meaning group gathers words for writing, art and books.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「字母」一词上的词；近义组收表示写作、艺术与书籍的词。

entries.definition: Written works valued as art, or the body of writing on a subject.
entries.definitionCN: 文学；文献；与 literary 同出拉丁语 littera。

entries.definition: Able to read and write.
entries.definitionCN: 有读写能力的；来自同一拉丁词干。

entries.definition: The ability to read and write.
entries.definitionCN: 读写能力；由同一词干加 -cy 构成。

entries.definition: Following the exact words rather than an intended meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 字面的；按字面理解的；同样来自 littera，但走的是另一条语义分支。

entries.definition: Set down in writing rather than spoken.
entries.definitionCN: 写下来的；书面形式的。

entries.definition: Showing creative skill and a sense of beauty.
entries.definitionCN: 有艺术性的；显出创造才能与美感的。

entries.definition: Relating to poetry, or having its beauty and rhythm.
entries.definitionCN: 与诗歌有关的；富有诗意与韵律的。

entries.definition: Fond of reading and study, or describing language taken from books.
entries.definitionCN: 爱读书的；书卷气的；也指从书本里搬来的语言。

normalIntro.en: The word is anchored in the Latin name for a letter, and its family keeps returning to reading, writing and the art of books.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词锚定在拉丁语对「字母」的称呼上，它的同族词反复回到阅读、书写与书本的艺术。

normal.en: Latin littera is a letter, so literature is writing made of letters and literary is what belongs to that writing.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 littera 是字母，所以 literature 是由字母写成的文字，literary 则指属于这种文字的东西。

normal.en: Literature and literary share one stem: the noun names the whole body of works, the adjective describes what belongs to it.
normal.cn: literature 与 literary 共用一个词干：名词指整批作品，形容词描述属于这批作品的东西。

normal.en: Literate and literacy also come from the letter, because knowing the letters is the first step into reading.
normal.cn: literate 与 literacy 也来自「字母」，因为认识字母是进入阅读的第一步。

normal.en: A literary agent handles books as a business, so the adjective also names the profession built around literature.
normal.cn: 文学经纪人把书当作生意来经营，所以这个形容词也指围绕文学形成的职业。

normal.en: Call a word literary when you meet it mainly in books, because the label records where the word still lives.
normal.cn: 一个词若主要是在书里遇到，就叫它 literary，因为这个标签记下的是它如今还住在哪里。

abstract.en: Letters are small marks that carry whole worlds, and literary is the adjective for the world built out of those marks.
abstract.cn: 字母是承载整个世界的小小记号，literary 就是形容由这些记号搭起来的那个世界。

abstract.en: A page can be read for information or for beauty; literary marks the second use.
abstract.cn: 一页纸可以为了信息去读，也可以为了美去读；literary 标出的是后一种读法。

abstract.en: Every literature begins with someone learning a handful of letters, which is why the same root also names literacy.
abstract.cn: 每一部文学都从有人学会几个字母开始，所以同一个词根也用来指读写能力。

examples.en: She has a keen literary taste and reads a novel every week.
examples.cn: 她文学品味敏锐，每周读一本小说。

examples.en: His account of the journey has a literary quality that makes it memorable.
examples.cn: 他对这次旅程的记述有一种文学性的质地，让人读过难忘。

examples.en: The literary agent read the manuscript and offered a contract.
examples.cn: 那位文学经纪人读完稿子，给了出版合同。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「里特瑞」——姓李的人特别爱读小说，身上有股文学的味儿；literary 就是文学的。

root: 拉丁语 littera（字母、文字）→ litterarius（与文字有关的）→ 古法语 literaire → 英语 literary；同族词多与字母、读写、文学有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is writing made of letters and valued as art; the senses divide into the art itself, its formal register, its crafted quality, and the profession around books.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是由字母写成、被当作艺术的文字；义项由此分出文学本身、它的正式语体、它的写作技艺，以及围绕书籍的职业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old novel open under a lamp, its pages softened by repeated reading.
core.cn: 核心意象：台灯下摊开的旧小说，纸页被反复翻读得发软。

branches.cn: 文学经纪人的桌上堆满稿件

branches.en: a word that lives only in books
branches.cn: 一个只在书里活着的词

branches.en: a sentence polished until it sounds like music
branches.cn: 一句话被磨到听起来像音乐

branches.en: a description that makes a plain road feel alive
branches.cn: 一段让普通道路活起来的描写

intro.en: A Latin word for a letter, its adjective, one French reshaping and two English suffixes carry literary from the alphabet to the art of books.
intro.cn: 一个表示字母的拉丁词、它的形容词、一次法语改写，再加两个英语后缀，把 literary 从字母表带到书本的艺术。

latinIntro.en: Littera and litterarius are recorded Latin words, and the adjective reached English through French before it was reshaped as literary.
latinIntro.cn: littera 与 litterarius 都是有记录的拉丁词；这个形容词经法语进入英语，后来才改写为 literary。
